sections.title: Introduction
Typical working process
Obtaining access to Arena
sections.text:
Arena platform is available at https://www.openforis-arena.org
Every user in the Arena platform has a specific role. These roles are described in detail in this chapter.
The platform limitations are as follows:
- The service is free and the maximum size of survey data is 10 GB.
- Only the Survey Administrator can view the survey data size.
- The maximum upload size of any file is limited to 1 GB.
In general, it is better to avoid uploading very-high resolution images into Arena, and to plan the amount of incoming data.
There are two methods to get access to Arena:
Method 1. Become a Survey Manager.
A Survey Manager can create a new survey and tailor it to meet your needs. You can also use ready-made templates to tailor your survey.
To become a Survey Manager, go to https://www.openforis-arena.org/
and click Create an account, under the Login button of the login page. Create your account before logging in, also if you want to sign in with Google or another external provider: only registered users can log in.
You will next see the following page:
Fill in all information. If you are dealing with forest resource data or are a first-time user with no experience with Open Foris Arena, it is recommended to start using a template: read more about them in this Annex. Then press Create account: you will receive an email with the link to confirm your email address and complete your registration (choose your password, or sign in with Google or another available sign-in option). Once your registration is completed, your role will be a Survey Administrator for your first survey. If you do not find the emails from Arena in your inbox, check the Spam/Junk folder, then add the sender (shown in the Create an account page) to your contacts or mark the email as not spam, so that the next emails reach your inbox.
Method 2. To get access to an existing survey, ask for an invitation from the Survey Administrator. This person can send you an invitation to new users by email. The Survey Administrator will specify your role in the survey.
____________________________________________________
When you have access to Arena, type in your email and password. In case you have forgotten your password, click Forgot password? to receive a password reset link by email (see Chapter 13). In the top-right corner of the login page you can also choose the theme (Light, Dark or System default) and the language of the user interface. At the bottom of the page there are links to the Arena website, to this user manual and to the support forum.
If you are a new user, set first your user profile: click on your profile picture in the upper-right corner of the screen and select My profile.
Here you can set up your title, name and profile picture. Read more about the user profile in section 3.3.

sections.title: Log in to Arena Mobile using QR code
sections.text:
Once you have logged in to Arena, you can easily log in to Arena Mobile by scanning a QR code generated by Arena.
To access this feature, you must click on your profile icon in the top right corner and in the menu that opens select “Login to Arena Mobile using QR code”:
A dialog like this will appear:
Open Arena Mobile and follow the instructions in the dialog; you will be easily logged into Arena, and you will be able to download your surveys and submit data to the server.

sections.title: User profile
Two-factor authentication (2FA)
sections.text:
Every user can protect their account with two-factor authentication: after typing the password, Arena asks for a verification code generated by an authenticator app on a mobile device.
To add a 2FA device:
- Open My profile and click Manage 2FA. The list of your 2FA devices opens.
- Click New, type a Device name (e.g. My phone) and click Create.
- Install an authenticator app on your mobile device (e.g. Google Authenticator or Authy).
- Scan the QR code with the authenticator app (or click Show secret key and type the key in the app).
- Type (or paste) two consecutive codes generated by the app in Authenticator code 1 and Authenticator code 2 (wait 30 seconds before the second code) and click Validate.
After the validation, Arena shows 8 backup codes. Save them in a safe place: they are shown only once, and each of them can be used only once to log in if you lose access to your authenticator device. Type copied and confirm to close the dialog.
When 2FA is active, after typing your email and password in the login page, type (or paste) the 6-digit Verification code shown by the authenticator app and click Verify. If you do not have your device with you, click Use a backup code and type one of your backup codes.
From the details page of a device you can also Regenerate backup codes (the previous ones stop working) or Delete the device.

sections.title: Signing in with Google, Microsoft or your organization's account
sections.text:
When the system administrators have configured external login providers (see 14.4), the login page shows a button for each of them under the Login button, e.g. Sign in with Google (under it, the caption Registered users only). Click it and sign in with your account at the provider: you are then logged in to Arena.
You can sign in this way only if you already have an Arena account or an invitation: the first time, Arena links the provider account to the Arena account with the same email address, if the provider has verified it. Email and password login is always available.
- Invitations: in the page opened from the invitation email, instead of choosing a password you can click a provider button (e.g. Continue with Google): the invitation is accepted and from then on you sign in with that account, even if its email address differs from the invited one.
- Two-factor authentication: if you use 2FA (see 3.4), Arena can still ask for your verification code after the sign-in with the provider.
- Arena Mobile signs in with email and password: if you have no password, set one with Forgot password? on the login page or from your profile.
In My profile, the Sign-in methods in the Sign-in & security section show whether you have a password and the providers linked to your account:
- Click Link next to a provider (e.g. Link Google) to sign in with it from then on: Arena opens the sign-in page of the provider and then returns to your profile.
- Click Unlink to stop using a provider; Arena sends you an email to confirm the change. The last sign-in method cannot be unlinked: first set a password (Set a password) or link another provider.
- If you can no longer use your provider account, click Forgot password? on the login page to set a password.

sections.title: AI features
Main user interface
sections.text:
The view in the Arena main window depends on your user role (see Chapter 11). With the full Survey Administrator’s access rights, the left side panel contains the following tools.
- Survey landing page - Management of survey properties; delete a survey; backup, export a survey; settings for map and security - Design or edit data entry forms - Visual view on survey hierarchy - Visual dependency tree - Management of categories (i.e., code lists) - Management of taxonomic tables (i.e., species lists) - Add, view, edit, clone, delete data - Data queries, and access to data cleansing - Map view & data editing; access to Earth Map and Whisp - Export data into Comma Separated (CSV) or Excel files - Import CSV/Excel/Collect/Collect Mobile/Arena backup data - Data validation report, and access to data cleansing - Create, edit, delete data processing chains, run RStudio - Show/stop RStudio Server (online process) - User management, invitation of new users - User grouping management -Link to this manual - Links to support materials and Arena repositories - List of latest changes in Arena - Terms of Service and Privacy Policy
- System Administration menus, shown only to system administrators at the bottom of the sidebar (see chapter 14)
Preferred user interface language in Arena: Automatically detected (from your browser settings), English, Spanish, French, Japanese, Mongolian, Portuguese, Russian or Serbian (Latin). The same menu is available on the login page.
Switch between the Light and Dark theme, or follow your System default. The same menu is available on the login page.
Lists work the same way in every page (surveys, records, categories, users...): click a row to open its item, to view or edit it. In the records list, where the rows can be selected, a click selects the row and a double click opens the record. With the keyboard, move to a row with Tab and press Enter to open it (Space selects it in the records list). In each row, the view/edit button (pencil, or eye when the item can only be viewed) and the delete button (trash) are the last buttons.

sections.title: Selecting and creating a survey (1/2)
sections.text:
In the upper right corner, there is access to the following functions:
Surveys page shows a table with all the surveys you can access. Select Only own surveys to show only the surveys you own, or type in the filter box to search surveys by name, label or owner. The list contains the following details.
Header | Explanation
NAME | Name of the survey. It must be at least 6 letters long.
LABEL | Label for the survey
OWNER | Name of survey administrator (owner)
DATE CREATED | Date when the survey was created
DATE LAST MODIFIED | Date when the survey was edited last time
DATE PUBLISHED | Date when the survey was published
STATUS | Draft: The survey is at the editing stage. It contains no data. Published: The survey is ready to store data. It can contain input data. Published-Draft: The survey is ‘published’, but there are unpublished changes in its structure (i.e., changes in attribute properties, new calculation scripts or setting).
NODES | Number of nodes. This indicates the size of the survey.
CYCLES | Number of cycles in the survey.
LANGUAGES | Languages in the survey (ISO 639 language codes)
RECORDS | Number of records in the survey (across all cycles)
FILES | Number of uploaded files (e.g. photos)
CHAINS | Number of processing chains in the survey
Click Visible columns to show or hide columns. Click Export to Excel to download the list of surveys.
New Survey allows a Survey Manager to create a survey in three ways: 1) Create a new survey from scratch, 2) Clone an existing survey or 3) Import a survey (Arena, Collect or ODK).
About naming of a survey:
- The name should only contain lower case letters, underscores,
- No space,
- No special characters (#%&"?).
The entry box will automatically ignore the wrong letters.
Next, some more information on how to create a new survey.
Method 1: Create a new survey from scratch. Fill in Name, Label, and choose the default language.
Next steps after creating a new survey: * Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and set in Description, needed Spatial Reference System(s) (SRS) and survey languages. * Create the survey structure using the Survey Designer, test your survey and then finally Publish it.
Method 2: Clone an existing survey.
Fill in a new survey Name and select a survey to be cloned. Cloning will only copy the survey structure, not the data. A cloned survey will always be in the ‘draft’ mode.
Next steps after cloning the survey: * Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed. * If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then Publish it.
Method 3: Import a survey. Import offers three options:
a) Import an Arena survey (.zip). An existing Arena survey, such as an Arena backup, can be imported back into Arena (with a new name).
b) Import an Open Foris Collect survey.
c) Import an ODK form (.xml).
Give first the name of the new survey in Arena. Check the Include Data box if the survey file contains data and needs to be imported, otherwise leave it unchecked. The file is uploaded in parts: if your internet connection is slow or unstable, select a smaller File upload chunk size.
Important: Do not use Export + Import (schema or backup) for cloning a survey! The reason is that a published and exported survey will stay published when imported back into Arena. This means that only a few changes are possible. Instead, if you clone a survey, the new survey will be in the draft mode, and you can, for example, change/edit a taxonomic list.
Next steps after importing the survey: * Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties if needed. * If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then Publish it.
An Open Foris Collect survey can be imported from a .collect, .collect-backup or .collect-data file. Note that after importing you should view the Collect Import Report at the Dashboard section. In addition, check out that all forms, tables, attributes and their properties are imported correctly.

sections.title: Selecting and creating a survey (2/2)
sections.text:
Follow these steps after importing a Collect survey: * Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed. * Use the Survey Designer to modify the user-interface (as location and size of text boxes etc.). * Go into Dashboard - Collect Import Report, and fix the remaining (unresolved) issues. * Test your survey in Arena and then finally Publish it.
An ODK form (XForm, .xml file) can be imported by selecting ODK (.xml) as Source: enter the Name of the new survey, select the .xml file and click Start import. The questions of the form become attributes, the repeats become multiple entities and the choice lists become categories; the labels are imported in all the languages of the form.
Before publishing the imported survey, check it in the Survey Designer: define the key attributes of the root entity (ODK forms have no key attributes) and fix the errors listed by Publish, if any (e.g. calculations that could not be converted into expressions). The data collected with ODK Collect can then be imported in Data > Data Import (see 9.9.4).
Note: after an update of Arena, the surveys may be upgraded in the background. If you open a survey while it is being upgraded, Arena shows the message “This survey is being upgraded, please retry shortly.”: wait a few moments and open the survey again.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.text:
The Dashboard section contains the following functions.
"Edit info" can also be accessed by clicking the survey name.
The Dashboard is a module of its own in the sidebar: open it from the sidebar or with Open dashboard on the survey landing page. It is available to the users who can at least cleanse records (it is not available to Data Editors).
Below the functions, the Dashboard shows a summary of the survey data. Select the period in Records added in the last: (e.g. 1 Year); the cards and the chart refer to the selected period:
- Records added in selected period: number of records added in the period; expand the card to see the number of records by workflow step (Data Entry, Data Cleansing, Data Analysis, all time).
- Contributors: number of users who added records in the period; expand the card to see the records added by each user.
- Storage: space used by the survey (shown only to users who can edit the survey); expand the card to see the space used by the files and in the database, out of the available space.
- Total records: trend of the number of records in the selected period.
- Map: shown when the survey has geo (polygon) attributes; it shows the polygons of the records, which can be filtered by owner.
- Sampling Point Data Completion: shown to users who can edit the survey, when the records are identified by sampling point data; it shows how many sampling points have been visited.
- Activity log: recent activity on the survey (e.g. records created or updated); shown only when the activity log is enabled on the server, to users who can edit the survey.
At the top of the Dashboard, the survey label is shown with its status (Draft, Published or Published/Draft) and the survey name:

sections.title: Edit info
sections.text: This section allows users to edit the metadata of the survey. The selections are divided into the following pages: Basic info, Branding, Map, Document Layout, User extra properties and Security. System administrators also see the Configuration tab, where they can set the total space available for the files of the survey (Files total space (GB)).

sections.title: Survey basic info
sections.text:
Basic info contains information about the following survey properties:
Name: Name of the survey in the database. A Survey Administrator can rename the survey.
Label: Label for a survey, a clear name for the survey.
View/Edit labels with other (selected) languages.
Description: Additional information about the survey (optional).
Field Manual Link: Full URL to the field manual of the survey (text) (optional). The URL must be publicly accessible.
Language(s): Survey language(s). If more than one language is added, then labels need to be given by all selected languages.
SRS: Spatial Reference Systems applied in the survey. Add here all SRSs which will be needed in the data collection. Hint: to add a new SRS, click the cursor into the input box and to see the options, type in some letters of the EPSG code.
Cycles: Inventory cycle(s) and timing(s). Note: survey times cannot overlap, so for example this data is accepted:
Cycle for Arena Mobile: The cycle for uploading a survey into Arena Mobile in a multicycle survey case.
The Map tab contains the areas of interest (see 6.1.6) and the sample-based image interpretation settings of the Map section, read more about it in this chapter.

sections.title: Branding
sections.text:
The ‘Branding’ tab lets survey designers customize the visual identity of a survey: its primary color, up to three logos, a background image for the survey landing page, and typography presets for the landing page title and description. Branding settings are saved with the survey and are published together with the rest of the survey definition, so data collectors and reviewers see the same branding once the survey is published.
Branding is entirely optional. A survey with no branding configured still displays a functional, unbranded landing page.
The Branding tab is organized as a form on the top and a live preview of the survey landing page on the bottom, so changes to colors, logos, background, and typography can be checked before saving.
Survey landing page
Branding is applied on the survey landing page, which is the default view when opening a survey from Home. The landing page shows the survey title and description (from the survey labels), a button to go to Records, and, when configured, the survey's branding: primary color, logos, background image, and typography presets. A separate button opens the Dashboard, which has moved to its own top-level module in the sidebar.
Primary color
The primary color is the main accent color for the survey. It is applied to key interface elements such as primary buttons and sidebar highlights, both on the survey landing page and while collecting data, so the tool matches the branding of the project or organization running the survey.
Set the primary color using the color picker or by entering a hex value directly (for example, #2E7D32). If an invalid color value is entered, the field shows a validation error and the branding form cannot be saved until it is corrected.
Typography presets
Typography presets control the text size of the survey title and description as they appear on the landing page. Choose the preset that best fits the length of the survey title and description and the overall look of the branding.
Logos
Up to three logos can be uploaded (Logo 1, Logo 2, and Logo 3). All three are optional and independent of each other.
Logo slot | Typical use | Displayed on
Logo 1 | Main survey / project logo | Survey landing page and header
Logo 2 | Partner or implementing organization logo | Survey landing page
Logo 3 | Additional partner, donor, or country logo | Survey landing page
To upload a logo, select Upload image for the relevant logo slot and choose an image file. Once a logo has been uploaded, the upload button for that slot is replaced by a preview of the image and a delete action; an existing logo must be deleted before a new one can be uploaded in its place. Logos that have been uploaded are shown, in order, on the survey landing page. Click an uploaded image to download it.
Landing page background image
A background image can be uploaded for the survey landing page. Background images are raster images (for example, JPG or PNG) and are limited to 5 MB. Use Upload image to add a background image and the trash icon to remove it; as with logos, an existing background image must be removed before a new one can be uploaded.

sections.title: Document layout
sections.text:
The Document Layout tab is available in Dashboard → Edit info to users who can edit the survey. It contains two groups of settings.
1) Document images
Images can be added to be shown in the header or footer of every printed document. Examples are an organization logo, a project banner, or a footer with contact details.
To add an image, click the + button. In the dialog that opens, set the following fields:
Field | Explanation
Label | Label of the image (required, in at least one survey language).
Place | Header or Footer (required).
Apply if condition | Optional expression. It is evaluated against the root entity of the record being printed. The image is used only if the condition is met.
File | PNG, JPG or SVG image, max. 5 MB. File names must be unique.
The document contains at most one header image and one footer image. For each place, Arena uses the first image in the list whose "Apply if" condition is met, or which has no condition. This lets you define alternative images for different cases. For example, you could use a different partner logo depending on the region of the record:
- Image 1: Header, Apply if: region == "north"
- Image 2: Header, Apply if: region == "south"
- Image 3: Header, no condition (used when neither of the above applies)
Click a row (or its edit icon) to edit an image. Images can be downloaded with the download icon and removed with the trash icon.
2) Layout options
Option | Default | Explanation
Header on first page only | Enabled | If enabled, the header image is printed only on the first page. If disabled, it is repeated on every page.
Page numbering | Enabled | If enabled, page numbers are printed on each page.
Note: as with other survey settings, publish the survey to make changes available to all users.

sections.title: User extra properties
sections.text:
User extra properties section allows users to define properties that can be associated with the users working with the survey. These properties can be numeric or text values.
Values can be assigned to the users in the Users list, pressing theicon in each row; in the dialog that opens, values can be specified for each user extra property:
User extra properties can be used in expressions like default values, validation rules etc., or to filter category items or taxa in the taxon attribute search. The function used to retrieve a user extra property is userProp and it can be used in default values, validation rules, items filter expressions etc.

sections.title: Security
sections.text:
Users who can edit the survey (Survey Administrators and Survey Editors) can view and edit the survey’s Security settings, as follows:
Meaning of “can view not owned records”: If enabled, then a Data Editor/Analyst can view all other users’ records in the survey (on the list of records). If disabled, a Data Editor/Analyst cannot view other users’ records in the survey.
Changes to the Security options take effect once the survey is published, as reminded by the message at the top of the tab.
The other options are the following:
- Visible in Arena Mobile, Allow downloading records from server to Arena Mobile, Allow uploading records from Arena Mobile to server and Allow uploading records with validation errors from Arena Mobile to server define if the survey can be used in Arena Mobile and how records can be exchanged between Arena Mobile and the server.
- Allow merging records with same keys (e.g. records created in different Arena Mobile devices): enabled by default. A record uploaded from Arena Mobile or imported with the same key values as an existing record is merged into it. If disabled, such a record is not imported and an error is reported.
- Notify survey administrators by email when records are uploaded from Arena Mobile: shown when records upload from Arena Mobile is allowed, disabled by default. If enabled, every Survey Administrator receives an email (in English) every time records are uploaded from Arena Mobile, listing for each record the key values, whether it is new or updated, the user who created it, the creation and last modification dates, the number of validation errors and warnings and its internal identifier (UUID), together with the user who uploaded the records and the date of the upload.
- Keep values of non-relevant attributes: when unchecked (default), during data entry the values of attributes that are no longer relevant are cleared, after the user confirms it. When checked, those values are kept in the record, even if the attributes are not relevant anymore.
- Allow data entry users to preview the draft (not published) form: when checked, the users who can enter data but cannot edit the survey (e.g. Data Editors) can preview the form with the latest changes not published yet, for example for user acceptance testing (see 7.2.9).

sections.title: Map
sections.text:
The Map tab contains the sample-based image interpretation settings (read more in 9.7.2), the areas of interest and the preloaded map layers of the survey.
Areas of interest
Areas of interest are polygons, for example the boundary of a forest reserve, of a stratum or of an administrative unit. They are used in expressions to check if a location is inside an area, or to find the area containing it. The expressions work also offline in Arena Mobile.
To add an area of interest, click Add. In the dialog that opens, enter the Name (used in the expressions) and optionally the Labels, then select a GeoJSON file (.geojson or .json, max 10 MiB) with one or more polygons in WGS84 coordinates. The polygons are shown on a map in the same dialog, so you can check them before clicking Ok.
For each area, the list shows the name, label, file name and number of polygons and vertices. Click a row (or its edit icon) to edit the area; use the other icons in each row to download its file, show it on the map or delete it. Show all on map shows all the areas together:
Click Save to store the changes. As with other survey settings, publish the survey to make them available to all users. The areas of interest can also be shown as layers in Data > Map.
The areas of interest are used with these expression functions:
- geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(coordinate, 'area_name'): distance (in meters) between a coordinate and the boundary of the area: negative inside the area, positive outside. For example, the validation rule geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(plot_location, 'forest_reserve') <= 0 checks that the plot is inside the forest reserve. Comparing the distance with the GPS accuracy, you can tell if a location is surely inside, surely outside or too close to the boundary to be sure.
- geoAOIContaining(coordinate): name of the first area of interest (in the order of the list) containing the coordinate, or nothing if no area contains it. For example, use it in the default value of a text attribute to fill in automatically the area where the plot is located.
Map layers shared with all the users of the survey (uploaded files or map services) are added in Data > Map, with the Add data menu.
Preloaded map layers
Preloaded map layers are map files (GeoJSON, KML or KMZ, max 10 MiB) distributed with the survey, for example the boundaries of the sampling units or the roads of the study area. Select Preloaded map layers enabled, click Add, enter the Labels of the layer, select the file and click Ok, then click Save.
The preloaded map layers are shown as layers in Data > Map and are downloaded with the survey by Arena Mobile, so they are available offline in the field. Use the icons of each row to download the file, show it on a map, edit its labels or delete it.

sections.title: AI policy
Publish a survey
sections.text:
A draft survey needs to be published to make all recent changes available for the users. These changes can be, for example, changes in attributes’ properties (as new validation rules), changes in form layout, new read-only attributes or new calculation scripts.
Publishing a survey will make the following changes to the survey:
- it will be available for data entry in the Data > Records section;
- changes applied to the survey will be visible even in data entry;
- deleted node definitions (e.g. attributes) will be permanently deleted from the records;
- modified validation rules will be evaluated again and records re-validated (only for changed/edited records);
- for surveys imported from Collect: record editing will be available.
When publishing a survey, there is the following warning at the screen.
If Publishing a survey fails, you do as follows:
- Open the Details section.
- Scroll into the end of the error list.
- Click on Export and you will get the error list into a CSV file (arena_NodeDefsValidationJob_errors.csv).
- Fix all issues in your survey and try to publish your survey again.
Changes affecting existing data
If the survey is already published and you changed something that recalculates values already entered in the records (for example the default value or the relevance condition of a published attribute, or an extra property of a category or taxonomy used in expressions), Arena shows a further warning, Existing record data will be updated, listing the affected attributes.
- Click Publish and update data to publish the survey and recalculate the affected values in the existing records. Values can be changed or cleared.
- Check Skip data update (not recommended) to publish without updating the existing data: the affected values are not recalculated until they are entered again, and the records may no longer match the survey definition. In this case, type the survey name to confirm and click Skip data update and publish.

sections.title: Export survey and data backup
sections.text:
The survey can be exported into a zip file with or without the data. In this way the user can create and download a backup file. The zip file contains the following content depending on the selected option:
Export Export + data (NO Activity Log) Export + data (Backup)
Activity log contains the history of a survey. For example, it can contain data about who and when a certain record attribute was updated with a new value, or who and when a record was upgraded from Cleansing level to Analysis.
It is typically faster to export a survey without the activity log.
The Export + data (NO Activity Log) option is shown only when the activity log is enabled on the server.
A survey containing a calculation chain and result attributes can be exported also without the result attributes (Export + data (NO Result Attributes), shown only if the survey contains processing chains). In this case, the exported file contains the survey structure and the input data.
The options with data are available only to Survey administrators; Data analysts and Survey editors can use only Export (survey without data), while the other roles cannot export the survey.

sections.title: Unpublish or delete a survey
sections.text:
In "Advanced functions", there are methods to unpublish a survey or delete it. Only users who can edit the survey (Survey Administrators and Survey Editors) can unpublish or delete it. Unpublishing removes all data from the survey but keeps its structure; to confirm it, you need to type in the survey name.
Deleting removes both data and the survey structure from the database. To delete a survey, you need to confirm the deletion by typing in the survey name.
After deleting a survey, you have no active survey selected. This means that most commands will be inactivated. If you go to the Home or Dashboard section, you will see the next text on the screen.
In order to continue working with Arena, you either need to select a survey or start creating a new one.
Clear activity log (shown only when the activity log is enabled on the server) deletes all the activity log data of the survey, reducing the space it occupies in the database. The input data of the survey are not affected. Also this operation must be confirmed by typing in the survey name.

sections.title: Collect Import report
sections.text:
If a survey was imported from an Open Foris Collect file, it gets a Collect Import Report. Otherwise, this option is not visible for a survey. The Collect Import Report button is shown in the Dashboard, after Advanced functions, to the users who can edit the survey.
The main difference between Arena and Collect is that Arena uses JavaScript (JS) language in expressions, but OF Collect uses XPath language (for example within Required and Validation rules). So, when a Collect survey is imported, all expressions need to be converted from XPath into JS, either programmatically or by typing them in manually.
After importing a Collect survey into Arena, the Collect Import Report table shows all expressions which need special attention, such as possible modifications. The import process can convert the most typical XPath expressions into JS, but not complex expressions. Therefore, it is essential to fix all remaining issues before trying to publish an imported survey.
The report table contains the following fields:
PATH: path of entity/attribute in the survey structure.
TYPE: expression type (Default value, Validation rule, Relevance, Required if, Parent code).
EXPRESSION: expression in Collect (Xpath).
APPLY IF: XPath APPLY IF expression in OF Collect.
MESSAGES: Validation rule’s user-tailored message in OF Collect.
View/Edit messages with other (selected) languages.
RESOLVED: If blank, the import process did not do the conversion. Check all unsolved issues before publishing your survey! Mark the issue "solved" (manually) after doing the correction.
Tick shows that the issue is solved.
Edit the table, form or attribute properties.
The report table can be exported into an Excel file by clicking the Export to Excel button. This is probably the best way to examine what needs to be fixed in the survey. In this table, the value ‘1’ in the column ‘Resolved’ indicates resolved cases, and those with blanks are not converted in the importing process.
Important:
A Collect survey can contain a validation rule which is logically incorrect but still working (!): a value is checked against an attribute that is given later on the form/table. An example: in Collect, the XPath validation expression is given for "Mechantable" (height) as follows:
In this case, the Collect Import Report shows this as an unresolved issue. The reason is that in this survey "tree_height (Height [m])" is after "Mechantable", as seen below in the table. Arena cannot manage a validation expression with an attribute being second in the hierarchy.
The second typical issue with a Collect survey is that Collect may not require setting in the key fields for multiple-entry entities. In Arena, all multiple-entry entities must have a key (or keys).

sections.title: Working with cycles
sections.text:
Arena can host multi-cycle data. By default, all new surveys contain ‘Cycle 1’. Users who can edit the survey can add, edit or delete cycles in Dashboard > Edit info (Basic info tab). Every survey needs to have at least one cycle.
After adding, editing, or deleting a cycle, the survey should be published to make the changes effective. Deleting a cycle will permanently remove all the records of the cycle!
When a new cycle is added, it inherits the survey structure (i.e. schema) from the previous cycle. However, data structure between the cycles can contain differences, so each cycle can have individual properties such as different attributes, form layout, etc.
If the survey contains more than one cycle, an attribute (with a specific name) can belong to one specific cycle, or to preset cycle(s). Attribute’s properties (e.g., name, label, validation rules) are the same across cycles, but an attribute’s position on the forms may vary.
More about cycles:
- Each cycle contains its own records. A record cannot be common across cycles.
- Settings for the Arena Map are common across cycles.
- Categories and taxonomies are common across cycles.
- Chains are common across cycles.
- The Validation Report is executed only for the selected cycle data.
- "Export + data (Backup)" will export data from all cycles.
- "Data Export" into CSV/Excel files will export data from the selected cycle. In every table, the first column indicates the cycle number.
- "Data Import" will import data only into the selected cycle.
- Within a published survey, records can be cloned from a cycle to a newer cycle (read more in Cloning data).
- Data processing with Studio can retrieve data from the Arena server only from the selected cycle, not all data across cycles.

sections.title: Compare a survey with another survey
sections.text:
With Advanced functions > Compare / update from file you can compare the current survey with another version of it and apply the selected differences. For example, you can design and test changes on a test server and then bring them to the survey on the production server, without exporting and importing the whole survey. The function is available to the users who can edit the survey.
To compare and update a survey:
- Export the survey without data (Export > Export) from the other Arena server.
- In the survey to update, select Advanced functions > Compare / update from file and drop the exported .zip file in the box (max 20 MB). Instead of a file, you can also select another survey of this server in Or compare with another survey on this server.
- Review the differences and select the changes to apply.
- Click Apply selected changes and confirm.
- The changes are saved as draft: test the form and publish the survey to make them effective.
At the top of the page you find:
- Select a new source, to discard the comparison and select another file or survey, and Refresh comparison, to compare the same file again with the current version of this survey (e.g. after editing it).
- Fingerprint: codes of the survey definition (draft) of this survey and of the compared survey. Equal fingerprints mean equal definitions. The first one includes the internal ids, so it is equal only for copies of the same survey; the structural one uses names and codes, so it is equal also for surveys with the same structure created separately.
- A summary of the differences: elements only in the compared survey, changed and only in this survey.
- Show only differences and Hide layout-only differences, to filter the lists.
The differences are grouped in tabs (Survey info, Node definitions, Categories, Taxonomies, Files); only the tabs with differences are shown. Select an element in the list to see, for each property, its value in the compared survey and in this survey. A label shows the status of each element (Only in compared survey, Changed, Only in this survey), and a warning icon marks changes that need attention, for example removing cycles from a published node definition, which deletes its data in those cycles.
Each element has a checkbox to include it in the changes to apply. Note that:
- Elements only in this survey are deleted if you apply their change, so they are never selected by default. If you select deletions, you have to confirm them by typing the survey name.
- Node definitions are matched by internal id or, when the ids are different, by name. When a node definition could have been renamed, use Match as renamed to apply the change as a rename.
- Some changes cannot be applied to a published survey, for example changing the type, the key or the multiple property of a published node definition: they are skipped and the reason is shown. Changes that depend on each other are applied together.
After applying the changes, a message reports how many changes were applied and how many were skipped. Publish the survey to make them effective.

sections.title: Survey
sections.text:
The Survey section contains the following tools:
- Form Designer *): tools for creating new data entry forms, creating and editing the tables/forms and attributes and all their properties, and to design the visual outlook of the forms.
- Hierarchy: Show the survey hierarchy, entities, and attributes.
- Dependency tree: Graphical tool that shows how attributes, calculations, validations, and expressions depend on each other within a survey schema.
- Categories **): Management of categorical data (i.e. code lists).
- Taxonomies **): Management of taxonomic data (i.e. species lists).
*) This is available for a Survey Administrator. **) Survey Administrator can add, edit and delete lists, other users can only view them.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.text:
Entity: Data entities are the objects of the data model such as ‘plot’ or ‘tree’. These are shown in Arena as forms or tables. Entities are containers for attributes and relationships between objects.
Attribute: A data attribute is a unit of information inside a data entity, i.e. it is a single-value descriptor for a data object. These are like properties of data entities: for example, an entity ‘tree’ can contain the following attributes: species, diameter, and age.
Node (object): A node is a basic unit of a data structure, and in Arena the data structure has the shape of a tree. A node object is represented by a single node in a tree, and it can be an element node, attribute node, text node, or any "node type".
A visual presentation of a survey is shown in the following figure.

sections.title: About the Form Designer user-interface
sections.text:
The Form Designer is a tool for designing the content and outlook of a survey. The Form Designer is a handy tool to create a user-friendly interface for data management. On the left, the page tree shows the pages of the survey (Only pages) or all its entities and attributes (All nodes); click an item to open it. Drag the handle on the right edge of the page tree to make it wider or narrower. The bar above the form shows the path of the current page; the copy button next to it copies the path (e.g. Cluster -> Plot) to the clipboard. Show names switches between labels and names of the nodes.
With the help of the Form Designer, you can do the following tasks with the forms:
Method | Icon | Explanation
Add a new subpage | add a new entity (table/form)
Define the number of columns | The default number of columns is 3, this can be changed [1 - 9]
Add a new object | add a new entity or attribute (+ button in the page toolbar)
Delete an object | delete an entity or attribute: Delete in the menu button of the object (☰), or Delete in its edit form
Rename an object | change the name of an entity or attribute in its edit form (pencil button)
Add/Edit objects’ properties | add/change all properties, such as label, default value(s), validation rules (pencil button)
Resize an object | Move the cursor to the lower right corner of the object, and then drag to resize: the objects below it are moved down to make room
Change the order of attributes | Drag to an object and drop it to a new place on the forms
Preview of the survey (desktop or Arena Mobile, see 7.2.9)
Move up/down | Move the selected page up or down among its sibling pages (page tree, Only pages view)

sections.title: Attribute data types
sections.text:
The properties of an entity (table/form) or an attribute describe the characteristics and behavior of data added to that object. The data type is the most important property because it determines what kind of data the field can store. Arena supports the most common data types applied in database management systems, and two composite data types: coordinates and taxonomic data. The data attribute types are presented in the following table.
Data type | Icon | Notes
Boolean | true / false yes / no
Code | refers to categorical variables (i.e., code lists). Read more at Categories Note: Arena creates two fields into the database: attributename and attributename_label
Coordinate | allows users to enter geographical coordinates Optional properties: accuracy, altitude, altitude accuracy
Date | entered in dd/mm/yyyy format
Geospatial | Allows users to enter geospatial data like polygons. It supports only GeoJSON format.
Time | entered in hh:mm format, or hh:mm:ss if Include seconds is enabled in the attribute properties
File | Allows users to upload a file (e.g. image, audio file, video, document, etc.). Optional property (image): show/hide geotag information
Integer Decimal | An integer is a whole number that can be positive, negative, or zero. Numbers with decimal digits. Default number of decimal digits: 6
Taxon | Read more at Taxonomies
Text | Allows users to add free text
Attribute data type conversion is possible. For example, you can change an attribute from Integer to Decimal. In general, conversion is possible only if the survey has not been published after creating the attribute; the only exception is the conversion of a published Integer attribute into Decimal (see 7.2.4.5). If the survey has been published, and it contains no data (=records), it can be unpublished and a data type can be converted then.
Note 1: When naming attributes, do not use the suffix "_label"! If for example you have a coded attribute cluster_district in the survey, there will (automatically) also be a field cluster_district_label in the database. If there is this type of conflict, this will be shown only when trying to publish the survey.
Note 2: Arena does not contain a data type "range" as applied in OF Collect. When a survey is imported from OF Collect, "range" type attributes are converted into two integer attributes: attributename_from and attributename_to.

sections.title: Description of properties (1/3)
sections.text:
The object's data type determines which properties you can set. Each data type can contain several properties which are expressed as parameters. Some properties are common for all data types, while others are unique to a specific type. Below is a list of properties with explanations.
This section is used to give the basic properties for forms, tables and attributes
Name | Entity (table/form) or attribute name in lowercase letters. Functions within the survey and variables in R processing use this name. For naming of entities and attributes in a survey for forest inventory, read more about "Naming of entities, attributes and variables" at openforis.org/materials The list of reserved words are as follows: asc, category, date_created, date_modified, desc, exp_factor_, file, id, length, node_def_uuid, owner_uuid, parent_id, parent_uuid, props_advanced, props_draft, props, record, record_cycle, record_step, record_uuid, step, taxonomy, unique, uuid, value, weight
Type | Data type (selected while creating an attribute; it can be converted into another type if the attribute has not been published yet; a published Integer attribute can be converted to Decimal)
Label | Label text
Description | Free text description (optional). There will be an info icon next to the label which will show the text put in description, as follows:
Label value [Boolean]
Allow only device coordinate [coordinate] | This applies only to Arena Mobile: if enabled, the user will not be able to modify the X/Y values, but he/she can only record the coordinate using the device GPS
Accuracy, Altitude, Altitude accuracy [coordinate] | This data can be read from Arena Mobile.
Max number of decimal digits [numeric] | Number of decimal digits
Category [categorical data] | Category table (i.e. code list) name. This allows users to edit a selected category table. This allows users to select or change the category table.
Parent Code [categorical] | Parent category (attribute) name for a hierarchical categorical data attribute
Display As [categorical]
Show code [categorical] | Show/Hide code
Text transform [text]
Text input type [text]
Include in records list | Show the attribute value in the list of Records
Taxonomy [taxonomic] | Species list name
Visible fields [taxonomic]
Vernacular name label [taxonomic] | Vernacular name in user-interface
Key | If enabled, this attribute serves as a unique identifier
Auto incremental | If an attribute is Integer and a key, it can be set increasing automatically by 1
Multiple | Allow multiple entries for this attribute. Note: These are difficult to use in data analysis, consider using multi-entry forms.
Max. file size (Mb) [file] | Maximum size of file to be uploaded. On Arena Mobile, if the file type is “image”, when an uploaded picture exceeds the specified maximum size, it will be resized to fit that value.
File name expression [file] | Expression is used to generate the name of the file when it is downloaded or exported as CSV/Excel data. E.g.: suppose that you have some attributes called “region”, “province” and “cluster_id”, the generated file name could be a combination of these 3: region + “_” + province + “_” + cluster_id The extension will be the same as in the original uploaded file.
File type [file]
Show geotag information (image file) | Geotagged photos are images that have geographical location data (latitude and longitude) embedded within their metadata. This allows users to see the coordinates and where a photo was taken on a map. Allow saving screen capture in map view (image file) If checked, the Map screenshot dialog of the map view can save the screen capture of the map in this attribute. Not checked by default; available only for image file attributes.
Cycles | If the survey contains more than one cycle, an attribute can belong to one cycle, or to preset cycles. Attribute’s properties (e.g. name, label) are the same across cycles, but the position on the forms may vary.

sections.title: Description of properties (2/3)
sections.text:
Included in cloned data | true/false. In a multicycle survey case, when a cycle’s data will be cloned to upper cycle, this setting defines whether this attribute data will be copied or not.
Vernacular name selection kept [taxonomic] | Enabled: when a taxon is selected using a vernacular (common) name, the specific vernacular name used for the search will also be stored in the data. Disabled: only the taxon code and scientific name will be stored, regardless of which vernacular name was used during the search. In Arena Mobile: Enabled: each vernacular name appears as a separate item in the search results list. Disabled: all vernacular names for a taxon are grouped together and displayed alongside the taxon (combined in a single entry). As a result, the autocomplete list contains fewer items.
Vernacular name always included if only one | Enabled: If this option is enabled and a taxon has only one vernacular name defined, that vernacular name will automatically be stored with the data when the taxon is selected. Disabled: only the taxon code and scientific name will be stored, even if the taxon has a single vernacular name.
This section is used to add default entry values, and conditions when a form table or attribute is applicable
Editability:
Always editable | This is the default option; the attribute will always be editable.
Editable if condition is met | If selected, the attribute will be editable only if the specified conditions (expressions) are met.
Read Only | If enabled, the entry can only get the default value (as from an expression)
Default values:
Default values not specified | Default values will not be applied.
Default values specified | Attribute value will be created using one or more expressions. Every default value expression is made by an “Expression” and an “Apply if” condition. See more about expressions in Chapter Expressions and expression editor and Examples of expressions. The first expression for which the “Apply if” condition is met will be applied. If there are multiple expressions, only the last one can have an empty “Apply if” condition; it will be applied if none of the previous ones are met.
Default value evaluated only one time | Disabled: the default value is re-evaluated when the source attributes change. This selection can cause problems, such as slowness with Arena Mobile. For example: if false, the autoincrement default value for tree_id will be recalculated repeatedly for every tree (in a table) when you add a new entry or delete a data row. Enabled: the default value is calculated only once.
Hide in entry form | If an attribute contains a default value or expression, then this attribute can be hidden in the entry form. A ‘hidden’ attribute value will be shown in the Data Explorer and included in the Data Export.
Relevance
Always relevant | By default, every attribute or entity is always relevant and applicable.
Relevant if condition is met | Function that determines under what conditions the field is applicable. When an attribute is read-only and is not relevant, it will not be calculated according to the default value expressions defined.
Visibility
Always visible | By default, every attribute or entity is always visible.
Visible if condition is met | Function that determines under what conditions the field is visible. A field could be relevant but not visible for some conditions, for example it could be hidden to some group of users. When an attribute is read-only but not visible, it will be calculated still.
Hidden when not relevant | If a relevant condition is specified and the condition is not met, the field is hidden on the form or table, otherwise it will be shown in light grey. If the field still holds a value (e.g. entered before the condition changed), it is shown in light grey also when this option is set, so that the value can be checked or deleted; Arena Mobile hides it anyway.

sections.title: Description of properties (3/3)
sections.text:
Always hidden | (available only for read-only attributes) the attribute will always be hidden from the users.
Items filter [categorical data] [taxonomic] | A JavaScript expression to filter the items from the category table. Read more in Examples of expressions.
Hidden in Analytical Dashboard | The attribute is shown/hidden as a Dimension on Arena Statistical Reporter app
Page orientation | Default (document): the entity uses the orientation chosen when the document is exported. Portrait or Landscape: the entity always uses this orientation, regardless of the choice made at export.
Hidden in Arena Mobile | If enabled, the entry (entity or attribute) cannot be seen on Arena Mobile. (Key and Required attributes cannot be hidden)
Include in multiple entity summary | Now in the Basic tab. If marked, the attribute value is shown in the entity selector (in Arena) and in the entity summary view (in Arena Mobile) (for a File attribute this cannot be set)
Include in previous cycle link | If marked, the value from the previous cycle will be shown on the data entry form (when the link to the previous cycle is active on the mobile app)
This section is used to automatically flag wrong entries during data entry. Using checks greatly minimizes data entry mistakes and facilitates data cleansing.
Min count -Multiple-entry attribute | Minimum number of entries allowed. Blank (default) = 0
Max count -Multiple-entry attribute | Maximum number of entries allowed. Blank (default) = no limit
Required
Not required | (default)
Always required | Arena displays as an error if the field is left blank
Required when condition is met | Arena displays an error when the condition is met and the field is left blank. If the condition is not met, no error is displayed.
Unique | Checks that the entered values are unique (not repeated) within a specified group of values. When an attribute is marked as Unique, its value must be unique inside the closest multiple entity (an error will be shown otherwise). E.g. in a structure like cluster -> plot -> tree, if you have an attribute tree_species marked as Unique, you can have only one tree per species inside the same plot.
Expression | Expression that defines the logic of the check. Read more here.
Apply if | Allows users to specify when the check is applicable (see an example below)
Severity | Error - blocks the data entry user from submitting the record to data cleansing Warning - assigns a warning flag to the record but does not prevent submission to data cleansing
Error message | Message to be displayed to flag error/warning, it should be robust and easy to understand (see an example in this Chapter)

sections.title: Attributes or entities advanced actions
sections.text:
Move the cursor upon the entity or attribute you want to edit, and an action button with the shape of an “hamburger” will appear; pressing that button will open a menu with advanced functions as follows:
Note: node move or convert is allowed only if the survey has not been published yet, or if the node is new and the changes have not been published yet. Exceptions: a published Integer attribute can be converted to Decimal (see 7.2.4.5), and attributes can always be cloned.

sections.title: Attribute or entity move
sections.text:
An attribute or an entity can be moved into another entity.
By clicking on the item “Move [attribute name]” in the advanced actions menu will open a dialog where the new “parent” entity for the selected node can be selected:
Select the entity where the node should be moved and confirm the selection by pressing the button “Move”.
Note: when moving an entity, only entities not descendants of the current one can be selected.

sections.title: Attribute clone
sections.text:
An attribute can be cloned into another entity. All its properties will be copied, including all the expressions defined for Default value, Relevant if or Validations.
The operation is similar to moving a node; by clicking on the item “Clone [attribute name]” in the advanced menu, a dialog to select the target parent entity will open; select it and confirm the target entity.
Note: since the cloning will copy the expressions defined in the source attribute, it may happen that some of these expressions will be invalid in the new cloned attribute; in that case, after the cloning, the attribute edit form will appear, thus allowing a fix of these errors.
Cloning is available to all survey designers, also for attributes that have already been published. Entities cannot be cloned with this function; to copy an entity from another survey, use Clone Node From Another Survey (see 7.2.4.4).

sections.title: Attribute data type conversion
sections.text:
An attribute can be converted from one data type to another. All properties that are compatible with the new type will be preserved, including expressions defined in Default values, Relevant if, Validations etc.
By clicking on the item “Convert [attribute name]” in the advanced menu, a dialog will appear, allowing the selection of the new data type as follows:
Select the new data type and confirm it by pressing the “Convert” button.

sections.title: Clone an attribute or entity from another survey
sections.text:
In the Form Designer, open the Advanced functions menu (top of the form) and choose Clone Node From Another Survey. In the dialog, expand the source survey's form tree to locate and select the entity or attribute to copy (either one can be picked, not entities only), then choose the Target entity in the current survey under which it should be inserted, and confirm.
If the cloned node (or any of its descendants, when cloning an entity) is a code or taxon attribute, Arena resolves its category or taxonomy automatically, without a separate step:
- If a category/taxonomy with the same internal ID or name already exists in the current survey, the cloned attribute is linked to that existing one instead of creating a duplicate.
- Otherwise, the category/taxonomy is cloned from the source survey automatically, and a notification lists what was cloned along with the node definition.
Note: the dialog lists the other surveys you can access and shows their published version.

sections.title: Convert a published integer attribute to decimal
sections.text:
Once an attribute has been published, its data type cannot be changed, with one exception: an Integer attribute can be converted to Decimal, for example when the field teams need to enter decimal values that were not foreseen.
Open the menu button (☰) of the published integer attribute: the menu contains Convert (besides Clone and Delete; Move is not available for published nodes).
In the conversion dialog, Decimal is the only target type available. Select it and press Convert, then publish the survey.
The values already collected are kept, including decimal values already entered (for example in Arena Mobile).

sections.title: Units of attributes
sections.text: Arena does not contain a property to set units for numerical attributes, nor automatic conversion between the units. It is therefore recommended to add information about the unit into the attribute’s label, such as "Diameter [cm]", "Area [ha]", etc.

sections.title: Automatically generating rows from category items
sections.text:
The rows can be automatically generated in a table, where the key attribute is categorical (code). The “Enumerate” can be set to the entity (i.e., to the table):
The rows will be generated using the items defined in the category of the key attribute inside the entity one row for each item). In the enumerated table or form, new rows or forms cannot be added or deleted, and the key code attribute will not be editable. In addition, the key attribute should not have an “Items filter” expression (because the items cannot be changed dynamically).
Note: a code attribute marked as “key” should be defined inside the entity, otherwise marking it with “Enumerate” will not make any effect.

sections.title: Dynamic enumerated entity
sections.text:
Enumerate auto-generates one table row per item in the key attribute's category and disables manual add/delete options. Until now that category always had to be used in full. Dynamic Enumerate adds an optional Enumerating items expression to the entity: when set, only the category items whose code is returned by the expression get a row; the rest are skipped. Leave it empty and Enumerate behaves exactly as before.
The expression is typically built around the unique() function, which returns the distinct values found in a multiple attribute or entity. This lets a table auto-generate one summary row per distinct value already present elsewhere in the record, instead of one row per category item regardless of whether it's used.
Example: a table_source table where the field team logs individual measurements, each tagged with a source_type code and a value:
- table_sum is set to Enumerate, linked to a category “types” (items A, B, C), with Enumerating items expression set to unique(table_source.source_type).
- As the user enters table_source rows, table_sum automatically gains one row for each distinct source_type actually used (not all of A, B, C, only the ones present).
- Each table_sum row can carry its own computed attribute, e.g. value_sum with default value sum(table_source[$context.sum_type == source_type].value), to total the matching entries.
Prerequisites
- The entity already meets the standard Enumerate requirements: multiple-entry table, Enumerate checked, with a categorical (code) key attribute linked to a category.
- The category linked to the key attribute must already contain an item for every code the expression can produce; enumeratingItemsExpression only selects among existing items, it does not create new ones. Values with no matching item are silently skipped.
- Like other node-def expressions, anything the expression references must be reachable from the entity's parent context, and the entity cannot reference itself (self-reference is rejected by validation).
Step-by-step
- In the Form Designer, select the multiple-entry table and check Enumerate.
- A new Enumerating items expression field appears directly beneath the Enumerate checkbox.
- Enter the expression, typically unique(<path to a multiple attribute>) - e.g. unique(table_source.source_type). Leave it empty to keep enumerating every category item, as before.
- Save the entity. While the expression field holds a value, the Enumerate checkbox is locked on; clear the expression first if you need to switch Enumerate off again.
- Test in Preview or a draft record: add/remove values in the source attribute the expression reads from, and confirm rows in the enumerated table appear and disappear accordingly.
- Publish the survey.
Behavior and limitations
- Sync is incremental, by design: adding a new distinct value creates one new row; removing the last row with a given value deletes only that row; rows for values that are still present are left completely untouched, including any data already entered in them. Editing an unrelated attribute does not touch the enumerated rows at all.
- Rows still can't be added or deleted manually, only the generated set changes, and only in response to the expression's source data.
- If the entity itself becomes inapplicable (e.g. via relevant when expression), all its enumerated rows are deleted, same as the existing Enumerate behavior.
- Unchecking Multiple, or clearing Enumerate, also clears the enumerating items expression.
- Same authoring and performance guidance as other Arena expressions applies: keep the expression simple, since it's re-evaluated whenever its source data changes.

sections.title: Summary on survey schema
sections.text:
The Schema Summary is an exported CSV or Excel file showing a summary about the schema. It contains the list with all entities and attributes, data types, labels, and selected properties (see the table below). The required column contains true, false or conditional; for attributes required only when a condition is met, the condition is in the requiredIf column. The hiddenInAnalyticalDashboard column tells if the attribute is hidden in the Analytical Dashboard.
A summary report can be exported from the Advanced functions menu at the top of the Form Designer, choosing. An example of a schema summary report is presented below.
Column | Explanation
uuid | (internal) universally unique identifier
name | name of entity / attribute
path | path in hierarchy
parentEntity | parent entity name
label_en | label text (English)
description_en | description text (English)
type | data type
key | key field?
categoryName | category table name (of code attribute)
parentCode | parent code (of hierarchical code attribute)
categoryLevel | category level number
enumerator | enumerator
taxonomyName | taxonomy table name
multiple | multiple entry?
readOnly | read-only?
fileType | file type
maxFileSize | max. file size
hiddenInForm | hidden in form?
hiddenInMobile | hidden in the Mobile app?
includedInMultipleEntitySummary | included in a multiple entity summary?
allowOnlyDeviceCoordinate | allow only to record coordinates of the device?
relevantIf | 'relevant if' rules
hiddenWhenNotRelevant | hidden when not relevant?
itemsFilter | items filter text
defaultValue | default value
defaultValueApplyIf | default value apply if (rule)
defaultValueEvaluateOnce | default value is evaluated just once?
required | is this required? (true, false or conditional)
unique | is this unique?
minCount | min. count (of multiple entities or attributes)
maxCount | max. count (of multiple entities or attributes)
validations | validations rules
validation_message_en | validation messages (English)

sections.title: Form language
sections.text:
Every survey can be defined in multiple languages. Languages can be defined in the Survey Info section (Language(s) field).
The users (using the web version or the mobile version of Arena) will see the data entry form in the language of their browser or their device.
When multiple languages are defined, a language selector dropdown will appear in the top bar:
By selecting a language, all the “labels” fields will be shown in the selected language.
When multiple languages are specified, every label field will have a small icon close to it: Pressing this icon will show all the labels in the languages specified for the survey and it will make easier their translation:
It’s always possible to add new languages and to remove existing ones, even when a survey is published and data has been collected already; this type of change will not affect or break the collected data.
To translate the labels outside Arena, use the items Export labels (CSV) or Export labels (Excel) of the Advanced functions menu: you get a file with one column per language. Fill in the missing translations and load the file back with Import labels from Excel or CSV.

sections.title: Form preview (desktop and Arena Mobile)
Multiple entities: automatic rows, summary and tables
sections.text:
Auto-create minimum items: for a multiple entity, this option (next to Multiple in the Basic tab) creates automatically, when the entity becomes relevant or its parent entity is created, a number of entities equal to the Min count set in the Validations tab.
Include in multiple entity summary (Basic tab of an attribute inside a multiple entity): the attribute value is shown in the entity selector of Arena (the dropdown used to choose, for example, a plot) and in the entity summary view of Arena Mobile. For attributes of the root entity the same option is called Include in records list and adds the attribute to the list of records.
In data entry, the rows of a table (multiple entity displayed as a table) can be sorted by clicking a column header: one click sorts ascending, the second descending, the third removes the sorting. Sorting by more columns is possible. The sorting only changes the display, not the data.
Read-only values in tables are shown as text (labels), not as input fields; long values are cut with an ellipsis.

sections.title: Other attribute properties and layout elements
sections.text:

sections.title: Expressions and expression editor (1/3)
sections.text:
Expressions are used to determine value. The resulting value is usually one of various primitive types, such as numerical, string (text), Boolean, or complex data type.
Expressions can be defined using the “basic” expression editor and an “advanced” editor; the basic editor is easier to use and allows to define most of the expressions you will need in Arena. The generated expression will be a JavaScript expression.
The basic expression editor lets users define binary expressions, such as variable == some_value. For each operand, users can specify whether it is a constant value, a survey attribute, or a function.
When Variable is selected, the user can select the variable/attribute from a dropdown list; when constant is defined, depending on the attribute where the expression is defined, the value can be inserted in a text field or selected using a dropdown list (e.g. if the attribute is a code attribute, the constant value can be selected among the possible values in the related category).
When a Function is selected, the user can select one of the custom functions defined in Arena and specify the parameters to pass to the selected function using a builder that depends on the selected function. The possible functions are listed in the following table.
Function name | Description
appId | Returns the identifier of the app editing the record: “arena” (Arena) or “am” (Arena Mobile). The app functions (appId, appIdLabel, appPlatform, appVersion) are evaluated when the record is created and again when it is edited with another app, platform or app version (e.g. a record created in Arena Mobile and then edited in Arena) Example: Apply If: appId() = 'am'
appIdLabel | Returns the name of the app editing the record: “Arena” or “Arena Mobile” Example: Read only text attribute with default value appIdLabel() and Default value evaluated only one time: name of the app that created the record
appPlatform | Returns the platform of the app editing the record: “web” (Arena), “android” or “ios” (Arena Mobile) Example: Apply If: appPlatform() = 'android'
appVersion | Returns the version of the app editing the record (e.g. “3.0.1”) Example: Read only text attribute with default value appIdLabel() + ' ' + appVersion(): app and version that edited the record last
categoryItemProp | Returns the value of the specified Extra Property of a category item having the specified code
count | Returns the number of rows that matches a specified criterion
dateTimeDiff | Returns the difference (in minutes) from two date-time couples
first | Returns the first value or node of the specified multiple attribute or entity
geoCoordinateAtDistance | Returns the coordinate at a specified distance and bearing from the specified coordinates
geoDistance Note: this replaced function “distance” in Arena 2.3 | Returns the distance (in meters) between the specified coordinates. The parameters can be constant values in the format SRID=srs_code;POINT(x y) (e.g. SRID=EPSG:4326;POINT(12.89463 42.00048) ) or variables referencing coordinate attributes, or also a call to categoryItemProp function to extract the location from a category (e.g. sampling point data category)
geoPolygon | Returns a polygon in GEOJson format. It takes a list of coordinate values as parameters (they can be constant values or coordinate attributes). E.g. geoPolygon(table.location) where “table” is the name of a multiple entity and “location” is the name of a coordinate attribute.
includes | Returns true if the specified multiple attribute includes the specified value
index | Returns the index (starting from 0) of the specified node among its siblings, e.g., returns the current table row (or form) index number
isEmpty | Returns true if the argument has no value specified Example- Slop percentage% Expression: 0 Apply If: isEmpty(plot_slope)

pow | Returns the value of a base raised to a power
recordCycle | Returns the cycle of the current record, as a number
recordDateCreated | Returns the creation date and time of the current record as a datetime value. It can be used in a text, date, or time attribute

userEmail | Returns the email of the logged-in user
userIsRecordOwner | Returns a Boolean value “true” if the user editing the record is also its owner, “false” otherwise
userName | Returns the name of the logged-in user
userProp | Returns the value of the specified Extra Property of the logged-in user
uuid | Generates a UUID (universally unique identifier) that can be used as an identifier (e.g., as a key attribute of an entity)
Depending on the selected Function, a function builder may appear, letting you select the parameters quickly (in the next image, the builder of the geoDistanceToAOIBoundary function, opened with the edit button next to the function name):
Arena uses the JavaScript Math object that allows users to perform mathematical tasks on numbers. Math is a built-in object that has properties and methods for mathematical constants and functions. See the full list of Math methods here.
For example, constants: Math.PI = approximately 3.14159
Math.E = approximately 2.718
and static methods:
Math.pow(x, y) Returns base x to the exponent power y Math.pow(2,3) = 8
Math.round(x) Returns the value of the number x rounded to the nearest integer Math.round(9.345) = 9
Strings are useful for holding data that can be represented in text form (see link to the String object). In JavaScript, a string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single or double quotes, and single or double quotes are the same thing. Some of the most-used operations on strings are to check their length, to build and concatenate them using the + and += string operators, checking for the existence or location of substrings with the indexOf() method, or extracting substrings with the substring() method.
For example:
"Sri" + " " + "Lanka" = "Sri Lanka"
aString= "Vienna"; aString.substr(0, 4) = "Vien"
aString.length = 6

sections.text:
Besides the functions listed in the table above, the following functions are available. In the basic editor, the list of functions shows a short description of each function.
- geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(location, 'area_name'): returns the distance (in meters) between a coordinate and the boundary of the specified area of interest: negative inside the area, positive outside.
- geoAOIContaining(location): returns the name of the first area of interest (in the order defined in Survey info > Map) that contains the coordinate, or nothing if no area contains it.

- prevCycleValue(attribute) and prevCycleValues(multiple_attribute): return the value (or values) of the same attribute in the record of the previous cycle. They work only in Arena Mobile, when the survey has more cycles and the link to the previous cycle is enabled.
Areas of interest. The areas of interest are polygons (GeoJSON format, WGS84 coordinates) that you add in Survey info > Map, each one with a name: use this name in the expressions.
