sections.title: Working with categories (1/2)
sections.text:
Categories define predefined lists of coded values that are used across the survey to provide consistent options for data entry, processing, and reporting. These fields are set up in accordance with pre-defined classification schemes. However, the Survey Administrator is free to add, remove or modify them. Code lists can be used to classify a wide range of attributes such as administrative levels, personnel, topographic elements, accessibility, land use classes, ownership and many more.
There can be two types of code lists: flat or hierarchical tables. A flat table contains only one level with two columns: code and label (or labels in all selected languages). A hierarchical code list can be used - for example - for storing data by administrative units (e.g., province, district, village).
Categories (and taxonomies) are shared across all cycles within a multi-cycle survey.
Command buttons
Import multiple category tables (UTF-8 CSV or Excel files) via a zip file.
Import a table from a CSV/Excel file.
Export the selected table into an Excel or CSV file.
Templates are practical examples (as CSV/Excel files) of how to build a category table for Arena.
1. Export a flat template file (for later importing your data). 2. ‘Generic’: export a hierarchical template. This table contains fields for extra properties. 3. ‘Sampling Point Data’: export a Sampling Point Data template.
The settings (gear) menu lets you: convert the category into a Reporting Data category (see below); convert it into the Sampling Point Data category (if the survey does not have one yet) or into a GeoPackage category (see 7.5.6); convert it back to a simple category; edit the extra properties definitions (Edit Extra properties).
Adding a new category
New code lists can be added in two ways: "manually" or by importing a table in CSV/Excel format.
To add a new code list, click on the button. Then type the Category name. The arrow next to the Add category button opens a menu to create a Sampling Point Data category or a category with geo capabilities (see 7.5.3 and 7.5.6).
The category names should be unique. If the category name exists, there will be an error message, as follows.
Code items are always text (upper-case letters are allowed). To start entering codes manually, click Add next to Items and fill in Code, Label and Description (optional). Items are shown as rows with index, code and label: click a row to expand it and edit the item, move it up or down, or delete it; click it again to collapse it.
A quicker option to create a new code list is to import them using a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file. The CSV file should be in Unicode (UTF-8) format. This is the format for a flat table. If the survey contains just one language, then the file contains three columns: code, label_[language], description_[language]

sections.title: Working with categories (2/2)
sections.text: While the manual process for adding code lists is perfectly legitimate and can be used for simple lists, for more complex lists (e.g. lists that have many items or with a hierarchical structure) it is strongly recommended to prepare them in advance and upload them into Arena by clicking the Import button.

sections.title: Extra properties
sections.text:
Category tables can contain extra information (i.e. Extra properties), and they can work as lookup tables. This ancillary data can be retrieved from other sources, for example from GIS.
Extra properties can be used for example in the "Items filter" expressions (Examples of expressions) and in data analysis with R.
The next image shows hierarchical data in a CSV file. This can be used to import ancillary data for clusters (level1) and plots (level2).
The extra properties can contain the following types of data: text, numeric or geometry point. In case of geometry point (i.e., coordinates), the spatial reference system (SRS) must be preset into the survey (see the Arena Dashboard section in this manual). A coordinate data split into three columns looks like this:
The best method of getting this type of ancillary data table into Arena is to create the table in MS Excel, Libre Calc (or equal), save it as a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file and then import it. While importing, Arena asks to select data type for each column because the default data type is ‘text’.
In the data analysis with R, all categorical tables are accessible (as a list of data frames).

sections.title: Sampling Point Data
sections.text:
Sampling Point Data (SPD) table is a special hierarchical code list with a fixed category name "sampling_point_data". It can be used to define the list of sampling points, and their properties such as coordinates of each sample’s location. Sampling point locations can be viewed on the Arena Map.
Here is an example of a Sampling Point Data for a forest inventory case:
SPD can be created easily by importing a CSV or Excel file that should follow the formatting indicated below:
- levelX_code columns: 1 column for each level X (maximum 3 levels, e.g. if you have 2 levels, cluster and plot, you will have a column "level1_code" with cluster id value and a column "level2_code" for plot id value);
- label_LANGUAGECODE columns: labels that will be associated to each item on the list; e.g. label_en for English, label_fr for French;
- description_LANGUAGECODE column: not needed, you can leave this blank!
- location_x, location_y, location_srs columns: geometry point data as shown above;
- optional: extra properties.
A spatial sampling point grid can be made in any GIS application, or by using a Plot Grid Generator, see Annex 6 for more information.
See the chapter Examples of expressions how to use and call Sampling Point Data with the help of expressions in a survey.
To create the Sampling Point Data category, you can also use the arrow next to Add category and select Sampling Point Data category: the category is created with the name sampling_point_data and the location extra property, so you only need to import the file. In the category editor, the label This is the Sampling Point Data category identifies it. If the Sampling Point Data category has no location extra property (e.g. it was imported without the location columns), the category editor shows the warning The 'location' extra property is missing: without the location, the sampling points cannot be shown on the map, exported to GeoPackage or analysed with Whisp.
Reporting Data tables
Reporting data tables can be used within analysis with R/RStudio (read more in Chapter 10). This is a flat or a hierarchical table with the last column containing area information (in hectares or acres).

sections.title: Clone a category from another survey
sections.text:
In Categories, use ‘Clone Category From Another Survey’ (next to Add category, Export all and Import categories in batch (from ZIP)). Pick a Source survey, then a Source category from that survey's category list, and confirm.
Arena checks the source category against the categories already in the current survey before cloning:
- If a category with the same internal ID already exists (i.e. this exact category was cloned into this survey before, even if since renamed), cloning is blocked with a message identifying it by its current name.
- If a different category already has the same name, cloning is blocked with a name-clash message.
- Otherwise, the category and its levels/items are copied into the current survey as a new, independent category.

sections.title: Export all category tables
sections.text:
All categorical tables can be exported into a zip file with button.
Choose Export to Excel or Export to CSV: the export runs in the background and, when it is completed, click Download to get the ZIP file.

sections.title: Categories with geo capabilities and GeoPackage export
sections.text:
A category whose items have a location (a geometry point extra property called location) has geo capabilities: the Sampling Point Data category is one of them. To create a category with geo capabilities, click the arrow next to Add category and select Category with geo capabilities; to add the location to an existing category, use Convert to GeoPackage category in the settings (gear) menu of the category editor. The location extra property of these categories is locked; use Convert to simple category in the same menu to unlock it.
The categories list shows the type of each category (Reporting Data, Sampling Point Data, GeoPackage) in the Type column. In the category editor of a category with geo capabilities, the Export to GeoPackage button exports the items, with their locations, into a GeoPackage file that you can open in a GIS application (e.g. QGIS). The export runs in the background; when it is completed, click Download. Items without a valid location are skipped.

sections.title: Whisp analysis of sampling point data
sections.text: For the Sampling Point Data category (with locations), the Generate Whisp analysis button sends every sampling point with a location to Open Foris Whisp for the analysis. Confirm the message: the analysis runs in the background and it can take several minutes, depending on the number of sampling points. The results are combined with the sampling point data and stored in a new category called sampling_point_data_whisp (if this category already exists, its content is replaced).

sections.title: Working with taxonomies (1/2)
sections.text:
This section allows users to add one or more species lists by uploading a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file. The list should contain all the taxonomic species that the user will select from during data entry. Species lists should be as comprehensive as possible and should be created using all resources available in the country: local or global databases, taxonomical books, experts’ knowledge etc. For security reasons it will not be possible to add species during data entry. Instead, additional species should be added to the CSV/Excel file (by a Survey Administrator) and the updated species list uploaded to Arena.
Taxonomies (and categories) are shared across all cycles within a multi-cycle survey.
Adding a Species list:
A species list table should be prepared in advance following the formatting requirements indicated below.
The columns are as follows:
- code (required): alphanumeric (i.e. letters and numerals) unique identifier code associated to the species,
- family (optional): family name of the species,
- genus (optional): genus of the species,
- scientific_name (required): latin name of the species (genus + [optionally] species name + [optionally] subspecies name e.g. Pinus spp. or Pinus radiata),
- lat (optional): synonym(s),
- vernacular_name (optional): such as local name or a timber trade name. The vernacular name column must be named with the ISO 639-2 language code of the corresponding language (e.g. eng for English, swa for Swahili, etc.). So, the column name in the imported file is just the language code. Vernacular names can be accessed in expressions with the “taxonVernacularName” function.
- extra properties (optional): all columns not corresponding to the previous ones will be considered as extra properties; e.g. ‘wood_density’, ‘species_commercial_group’, ‘protection_class’, etc. Extra properties can be accessed in expressions with the “taxonProp” function or can be used in the "Items filter" expressions (Examples of expressions) and in data analysis with R.
An example of a valid (tree) species list:
Optionally, the Survey Administrator can specify other columns, such as the vernacular names of the species using the language code (in 3 characters ISO-639-2 format, e.g. 'swa' for Swahili, 'eng' for English) as header of these columns. Multiple values are allowed for vernacular names, and they need to be separated with a slash ( / ) character.
Note: a species name (in the scientific_name column) can exist only once in the table. Similarly, each scientific name should have a unique species code.
To add a new taxon list, specify first a name for the list in Arena. Then click Import, select the CSV/Excel file and click Back when ready. The screen will now show the records present in the species list. Species lists can also be renamed, deleted or exported. If needed, additional species lists can be created and uploaded in the same manner.
There are two species names automatically added to your list by the system: Unknown (UNK) and Unlisted (UNL). Avoid entering the same names and codes into the survey.
Taxonomic tables can contain extra properties associated with the species, e.g. dry wood density, timber price, minimum cutting diameter, etc. (see the previous figure with an example containing "wood_density" as an extra property). Extra property columns can be imported only via reading in a CSV or Excel file.

Using a template
sections.text:
Templates are surveys which can offer an easy way to start designing a new survey. They are tested surveys which will fit to specific purposes, such as for forest inventory or socio-economic survey data collecting.
More about the templates:
- Only users who can create surveys (Survey Managers and System Administrators) can create a survey from a template
- The idea of using templates is that it is easier to delete tables, forms and attributes than create them. Therefore, there are more entities and attributes in these templates than needed!
- Survey labels are already stored with multiple languages. All labels can be edited as needed, and new language(s) can be added.
There are the following templates available in Arena. Please see Annex 4 containing screenshots of these templates.
