- Click the Create Survey button. The new survey is created and opened in the Dashboard.
- Select in the Dashboard and edit the survey properties. You can still change the survey name here. You can also delete all unneeded languages and add the required spatial reference systems into the survey.
- Go into the Form Designer, and edit the survey as needed. You can delete the unneeded entities (tables/forms) and attributes and add new ones into the pages.
Templates typically include more entities and attributes than are needed for a specific survey, as it is usually quicker to remove unnecessary elements than to add new ones.
- Test your survey with Preview.
- When ready, Publish the survey.
- Go to Users and invite users to get access to your survey (see more at the chapter "User roles and invitation to access a survey").

sections.title: Getting a new template into Arena
sections.text:
Currently, only System Administrators can add new templates to Arena (see 8.3). If you are a Survey Administrator and would like to propose a new template or suggest improvements to an existing one, please contact the Arena development team at openforisinitiative@gmail.com. Include “Suggested survey to Arena template” in the email subject line.
A template is typically based on a published and tested survey and should be sufficiently generic to support a specific data collection purpose. As noted earlier, a well-designed template may include more attributes than are required for a particular survey, since removing unnecessary attributes is usually easier and faster than adding new ones in the Form Designer.

sections.title: Creating and managing templates
sections.text:
System Administrators can create templates and manage them from the user menu (click your profile picture at the upper-right corner):
- Templates: lists the templates (select Only own surveys to see only yours). Select a template to open it: you can then edit it like any survey (Form Designer, categories, taxonomies, etc.).
- New Template: creates a new template, from scratch (New Template From Scratch) or by cloning an existing template or survey (Clone). Give it a name and click Create Template.
A template must be published before it can be used: only published templates are listed under Clone from > Template when creating a new survey. Write a clear label and a description in Edit info: they are shown in that list and help users choose the right template.
Processing chains can be cloned from templates too: when you clone a chain from another survey, the published templates that contain chains are listed in the Templates group (see chapter 10.6).

sections.title: What are the data entry stages?
sections.text:
Arena implements a workflow which divides data processing into three steps (or stages): 1) data entry, 2) data cleansing, and 3) data analysis.
- Data entry stage
- Enter data exactly as recorded on the field forms.
- Data are neither interpreted nor corrected during this phase.
- Invalid values (those marked as "error") must be checked against the field forms. If the value was copied correctly, the value should be manually accepted. If it was copied incorrectly, the value should be entered as it appears on the field forms.
- Once all errors are either resolved or confirmed, the data entry clerk submits the record for data cleansing. Before entering the cleansing phase, a copy is made and marked read-only. No further changes may be made to this record by data entry staff (unless the record is returned by data cleansing staff).
- Data cleansing stage
- Experts with knowledge of field conditions and data work with a copy of the data entered at step 1 to correct or remove invalid values. Note: "Data entry" level users cannot edit the data which is at the cleansing stage.
- If the data cleansing expert deems that the data entry task was not completed or that the record contains too many errors, the record may be returned to phase 1 (entry) for additional changes.
- Once all data errors are resolved, the record may then be submitted for data analysis. This locks the record so that no further changes may be made.
- Data analysis stage
- Records are locked. They can be viewed but not edited.
- Records ready for analysis.
- If during analysis data are deemed incomplete or incorrect, the record may be rejected and sent back for further cleansing. Once updated and resubmitted, the record may once again be available for calculation and analysis.
In the record editor, the current step is shown at the upper-right corner (e.g. Step 1 (Entry)). Click the arrow on its right to submit the record to the next step, or the arrow on its left to send it back to the previous step. Arena asks you to confirm.
In the Data/Records view, selected records can also be promoted or demoted with the Update records step menu, as follows:

sections.title: Adding, editing and viewing records (1/2)
sections.text:
The Records section is used to enter, edit, view, and delete survey data. The main records view lists all root-level records and displays key metadata such as key field values, creation and modification dates, step, and the number of errors and warnings. Click a row to select it and double-click it to open the record.
The steps (=stages) are coded as follows: 1: Data entry stage, 2: Data cleansing stage, 3: Data analysis stage.
The command buttons on the right side are as follows:
Edit a record. Delete a record. View a locked record.
In the top left corner, the table has a checkbox to select all records in the view. If you have more than the currently set number of records in the view (i.e., 15, 30, 50 or 100), this method will just select the records of the current page (and not all your records).
Records can be displayed either unsorted or sorted , as follows:
Unsorted Descending order Ascending order
The user interface offers an input box for filtering the records, as follows:
The list of records can be exported into an Excel file by clicking on the button.
The Export button opens a menu with these options:
- Export list: the list of records, as shown in the table, as an Excel file.
- Export data: the data of the records as CSV files (see Data export).
- Export data summary: a summary of the data of each entity (for users who can analyse data).
- Export selected records (Arena format): available when records are selected. The selected records, with their files, are exported as a ZIP file in Arena format, that can be imported in Arena (see Import data from Arena/Arena Mobile file) or in Arena Mobile.
Selected records are kept when you move to another page of the list, so you can select records on several pages. The number of selected records is shown at the bottom left of the list. The selection is cleared when you change the filter or the number of records per page.
Dates and times (e.g. Date created and Date last modified) are shown in the time zone of your browser.
Data entry is straightforward. You will see all tables/forms at the left side panel, and data entry form in the main window at the right side. Start always entering data at the highest hierarchical level. For example, if you want to save forest inventory data where the structure is "cluster-plot-tree", input the cluster level data first, then the plot level etc. This helps ensure data consistency.
Arena does not lock the records (at data entry stages 1 and 2): users can work with the same data set, even edit the same record simultaneously. All records are locked only when data are submitted to stage 3 (Data Analysis). To avoid accidental changes, a record opened from the list is shown read-only: click Unlock at the top of the form to edit it (and Lock to go back to the read-only view). A new record opens ready for editing.
Start adding a new record by clicking button. The program will open a data entry form. While entering the data, all data are automatically written into the database, i.e. there is no ADD-button!
All items that are set as "required" are marked with a red symbol as long as the input field stays blank. The red label text and the red symbol can also indicate that there can be an error in the data item. In this case, Invalid record is shown at the top of the form: click it to open the validation report of the record.
In case of a multiple-entry table/form, such as tree data, the new record can be added by clicking the button next to the table/form’s name. In tables, read-only values (e.g. calculated attributes) are shown as labels, and long values are cut with an ellipsis (…).
There are two ways how to see the entities and attribute identifiers:
entity (table/form) or attribute name is shown,
entity or attribute label is shown.

sections.title: Adding, editing and viewing records (2/2)
sections.text:
When working with forms that belong to lower-level entities, there is a text in the upper left corner showing the position of the record in the survey hierarchy (click the copy icon next to it to copy this path to the clipboard), as follows:
Species data entry can be handled so that you start typing in the first letters of the species name, or a code. Then a dropdown menu will emerge, and you can pick up the correct name as shown in the next image.
There are two species names automatically added by the system when a taxonomy is imported from a file: Unknown (UNK) and Unlisted (UNL). In order to enter one of these, type ‘un’ into the species name input box.
When attribute data type is ‘file’, the user interface looks as follows:
This is an upload button that can be used to upload a file into the Arena database.
When a file has been uploaded, Arena shows the file name. When hovering over the name, a small snapshot view becomes visible, and when clicking the file name it can be downloaded into the local machine.
When a change makes some fields no longer relevant (their relevance condition is no longer met), Arena lists them and asks you to confirm that their values will be cleared. Click Ok to clear them, or Cancel to undo your change. If the values of non-relevant fields must be kept, a survey administrator can select Keep values of non-relevant attributes in Survey Info > Security.
In the entity selector of a multiple entity shown as a form (the dropdown used to choose, for example, a plot), an icon next to each entity shows its status: errors, warnings or complete. In the page tree of the form, the page of a multiple entity shows the status of the selected entity.

sections.title: Deleting a record
sections.text:
If you need to delete a record, go to the Records section and view the list of records. You can select one or more records and delete them by clicking the trash icon in their row or, after selecting them, the button.
Look always at the step of your record: you can only delete a record that is on the Entry or Cleansing stage. After clicking on the Delete button, the following message box will appear.

sections.title: Deleting a row in a table
sections.text:
A row of a table can be deleted as follows: browse to the last column of a row. There you will see a trash box icon. Click that and message box will appear:
You can click Ok if you are sure. But be aware: there is no UNDO function in the system!

sections.title: Cloning data
Data Explorer and aggregating data (1/2)
sections.text:
Data Explorer is a tool for viewing data in the tabular format. You can view both input data and (computed) result variables in the same table. You can view data in multiple ways (such as filtered and/or sorted), and it can be exported into a CSV or Excel file. In Raw mode, users who can edit the data can also turn on Edit and edit the data directly in this view.
Data Explorer can be used to aggregate data. This means that it can work as a reporting tool in "Aggregate Mode".
Letter "M" indicates that this is a multiple-entry attribute.
Multiple-entry file and taxonomic attributes are not listed with the attributes of their entity: select them in the entity selector to view their values, one per row.
All data in view can be exported into a CSV or Excel file with the Export button.
The main controls of Data Explorer are:
- Entity selector (left panel): select the entity (table) to view. The funnel button next to it filters the attributes by data type; Search variable by name filters them by name or label.
- Attributes list: click the attributes to add them as columns. They also appear as chips above the table, where you can remove them or drag them to change the order of the columns.
- Show/Hide Node Definitions Selector button: shows or hides the left panel.
- Mode: Raw (one row per entity) or Aggregate (see below). In Raw mode, the Edit switch lets you edit the data in the table.
- Filter records, Sort and Export: filter, sort and export the data in view. You can also sort quickly by clicking the arrow next to a column header.
- View: display options (Show names, Show codes, Show total and percentage).
- Manage queries: save the current query (entity, attributes, filter, sorting) and open the saved ones.
- Table / Chart: show the data as a table or as a chart.
The current version allows users to view and export the computed result variables in the Data Explorer view. Similarly, as imputed data attributes, computed result variables can be selected into the view, as below.
Data can be aggregated to higher levels of the hierarchy. The aggregate mode contains two sections:
- Dimension. All categorical, boolean and key attributes of the selected entity and its parent entities. The list also contains computed categorical variables, and these are tagged with (C).
- Measure. All numeric attributes of the selected entity and its parent entities but excluding key attributes. The list also contains computed quantitative (i.e. numeric) result variables, and these are tagged with (C).
Multiple-entry attributes cannot be shown in the aggregate mode view.
For example, tree result variables, such as "number of trees per hectare" can be aggregated to a plot level, or any upper level.
Follow the next steps to see the aggregates:
- Select the entity (table) to report in the entity selector
- Click Aggregate next to Mode.
- Select the Dimensions to be reported. In this case Cluster ID and Plot no. are selected:
- Select the Measures to be reported.
- In the table, Sum is the default function. To change it, click the gear icon in the column header at the icon and change the aggregate function.
Deselect Sum and select Average and Count.
And then close the Aggregate function window by clicking button at the top-right corner (or Close at the bottom). In the result view, the DBH statistics look as follows:

sections.title: Data Explorer and aggregating data (2/2)
sections.text:
- More complex custom aggregate functions can be applied in the reporting, if needed. The aggregation uses the Structured Query Language (SQL) expressions which is the fastest method to run a database query on the Arena server. In the aggregate functions panel, click New under Custom aggregate functions, enter a name and an SQL expression using the column names of the entity (e.g. dbh), then click Save. The expression can contain only the column names of the entity, numbers, text in single quotes, arithmetic and comparison operators, CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END, FILTER (WHERE …) and common functions (e.g. sum, avg, count, min, max, median, stddev, percentile_cont, coalesce, round): any other SQL (e.g. SELECT, semicolons or comments) is not accepted and the error is shown on the expression field.
After clicking Save, we can see the list of custom aggregate functions as follows:
The reported custom aggregates need to be selected (checkbox) in order to see them in the report table.
- Click Close.
And the results will look as follows:
- Data can now be exported to a CSV or Excel file with the Export button .

sections.title: Filtering records and searching attributes
sections.text:
Click Filter records to show only the rows matching an expression. Build the expression with the basic editor (variable, operator, value, +AND, +OR), or click Advanced to write it. Expressions are written in JavaScript syntax, using the attribute names: e.g. dbh >= 40 && total_height > 20. Use && for AND, || for OR, == for equal and != for not equal.
To search text values, use text_attr.includes('abc'), text_attr.startsWith('abc') or text_attr.endsWith('abc'). Add .toLowerCase() before them to ignore the case, e.g. text_attr.toLowerCase().includes('abc'). Press Ctrl+Space to see the variables and functions you can use.
Click Apply to filter the data. While a filter is active, the Filter records button is highlighted. The same filter is used when you export the data.
To find an attribute quickly in a long list, type part of its name or label in Search variable by name, above the attributes list.

sections.title: Totals and percentages
sections.text:
In aggregate mode, with a single measure, you can show the total of the measure and the percentage of every row. Open the View menu and select Show total and percentage: a % column is added next to each aggregate function and a Total row at the bottom of the table.
The View menu also contains:
- Show names: show the attribute names instead of their labels.
- Show codes: show the codes of the category items next to their labels (table view only).

sections.title: Exporting data as a table or as a data matrix
sections.text:
Click Export to export the data in view. Choose the file format (Excel or CSV) and the options, and click Export. The options include Records modified after and Records modified before, to export only the records modified in a period.
When the selected entity is a multiple entity (e.g. trees, or species of a vegetation plot) and you are in Raw mode, you can also export the data as a Data matrix: one row for each species (or other attribute) and one column for each record, as required by vegetation analysis tools such as Turboveg, Juice and Synbiosys. In Export as, select Data matrix, then choose:
- Rows: the attribute whose values become the rows (e.g. the species). Taxon attributes are exported with their scientific name.
- Second row attribute (optional): e.g. the layer, when the same species can appear more than once in a record.
- Key attributes used to name the record columns: each record becomes a column, named after the values of the selected key attributes (at least one).
- Values: the attribute shown in the cells (e.g. cover).
The Preview shows the structure of the exported table. If a filter is set in Data Explorer, only the matching data is exported. Click Start export to generate the file.

sections.title: Charts
sections.text: Click Chart to show the data as a chart (bar, pie, line, area or scatter chart). Charts also work with large data sets: when there are too many items, the chart shows a random sample of them that always includes the outliers, and a message tells how many items are shown out of the total.

sections.title: Viewing map data
sections.text:
If a survey contains a Sampling Point Data table or coordinate data, the locations of the points can be viewed on a map in Data > Map. Point locations can also be recorded using the map view. Base map data can be only viewed but not exported from Arena.
The map opens in a workspace with the following parts:
- the top bar, with the Base map, Add data, Display and Tools menus, the Screenshot, Zoom to data and Full screen buttons, and a search box;
- the side panel, with the Layers, Records and Legend tabs (the arrow button collapses the panel);
- the status bar, at the bottom of the map.
By clicking on a map marker, you open a pop-up window with the location of the point and the "Edit record" button, which opens the record in a floatable form window on top of the map view. The Previous / Next arrow buttons of the pop-up move to the previous / next record of the layer.
Markers in each layer have a different colour, assigned randomly: click the colour dot next to a layer in the Layers tab to change it. Use Display > Marker labels to show or hide the markers’ labels; Display > Location markers shows or hides the markers. The label contains the values of the key attributes separated by a hyphen (e.g., cluster_id - plot_no, 1 - 1 in the map view above).
The markers (points) of the selected layers will be shown grouped in clusters. Each cluster of points is a circle with the number of grouped points. Clicking on the cluster or zooming sufficiently the actual locations will be visible as follows:
With the Base map menu, you can select the base map from several options (custom base maps added as WMS / WMTS services or XYZ tiles are listed there too, see 9.7.5). In the Layers tab, select the layer(s) to be shown: there is one layer for each coordinate attribute defined in the survey (Input data), one for each level of the Sampling Point Data and one for each area of interest of the survey (see 9.7.8).
The maximum zoom levels are as follows: ‘ESRI World Imagery’ 17, ‘ESRI Topographic’ 16, ‘ESRI Terrain’ 9, ‘UN ClearMap’ 8, and ‘UN ClearMap with labels’ 6.
Use the search box in the top bar to move the map to a location or to a record. Type coordinates in decimal degrees (e.g., -6.1295, 37.587), in degrees, minutes and seconds (DMS) or in UTM (e.g., 37M 343814 9322016) and press Enter; or type the beginning of a record key (e.g., 1) and select the record in the list. The search finds the records of the layers shown on the map.
The Zoom to data button zooms the map to the data of the layers shown, and the Full screen button shows the map workspace on the whole screen (press Esc or click the button again to exit).
The Records tab lists the records of the layers shown on the map, grouped by layer, with the number of markers. Click a record to move the map to its location and open its pop-up; use Sort to sort the list by key. The selected record is highlighted in the list. Drag the handle on the right edge of the panel to make it wider or narrower.
The Legend tab explains the symbols on the map: record locations, groups of nearby records, the sampling polygon and the UTM grid (when shown) and the added layers.
In the record editor, the map button next to a coordinate attribute opens the location in a smaller map, with the Base map and Display menus, the measure distance tool and a coordinates search box. Click the marker to see the coordinates and the elevation of the point; double click on the map or drag the marker to change the location (if the record can be edited), then click Save.
The status bar at the bottom of the map shows the coordinates of the mouse pointer (click the notation, e.g. Lat, Lon, to switch to DMS or UTM), the current zoom level, the scale and the number of records in view:

sections.title: Sample-based image interpretation
sections.text:
The sample-based image interpretation allows users to visually collect data from map and satellite images using sampling polygons and a set of control points. The settings are in Survey info, Map tab (check Sample-based image interpretation enabled).
There are two shape options: rectangle and circle.
A rectangular sample plot. Note: Latitude is the Y axis, longitude is the X axis on a map.
A circular sample plot:
The UTM grid is displayed in the map view.
The control points are shown as small coloured polygons in a grid inside the sampling polygon. These are clickable: by clicking a point you can change its colour (with 5 colour options). The control points can be used to assess land or land cover features, such as proportions of land-use categories, forest coverage, etc.
In the map, use the Display menu to show or hide the Sampling polygon, the Control points and the Plot reference point (section Image interpretation, available when sample-based image interpretation is enabled), and the UTM grid.
Offset North/East moves the sampling polygon and the control points to the desired direction and distances. The "plot reference point" is an optional feature. This is a red point that can be used to mark for example a plot center point, if a grid is shifted with "offset" values.
There are two methods to collect the data: 1) using a Sampling Point Data table, or 2) imputed records with coordinate data.
When you click on the plot marker icon, Arena opens a pop-up window showing the following information.
Sampling Point item: Level code (in the Sampling Point Data), coordinates, elevation, ‘Create new record’ button (is available if the survey is published after the latest changes), Previous (<=) / Next (=>) buttons: move to the previous/next item in the Sampling Point Data table.
A record with a coordinate data: record’s key attributes, coordinates (SRS as in imputed data), elevation, owner of the record, ‘Edit record’ button, Previous (<=) / Next (=>) buttons: move to the previous/next record on the record list. Buttons to access Open Foris Earth Map and Whisp
In the Edit Record view, this button opens a floatable browser window that can be moved (to be shown on a second monitor).
It can happen that the maximum zoom level is reached and the markers are still clustered, meaning that the points are very close to each other or overlapping. Then clicking on a clustered marker opens a pop-up showing a list of points in this cluster, and you can select the preferred item.

sections.title: Google Earth Engine queries via Earth Map
sections.text:
Earth Map (EM) is a free Open Foris tool developed by FAO in the framework of the FAO – Google partnership. It allows users to easily visualize, process and analyze multi-temporal satellite imagery and global datasets on climate, vegetation, fires, biodiversity, geo-social and other topics, using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) data without coding. Users need no prior knowledge of remote sensing or Geographical Information Systems (GIS).
Currently, we can make a GEE query for a polygon in EM. The polygon submitted from Arena is the same as defined in the survey settings, see Sample-based image interpretation. This polygon is called Area of Interest (AOI) in Earth Map.
If sample-based image interpretation is not enabled in Survey info (Map tab), then Arena submits a polygon of 100m x 100m to Earth Map.
The following picture shows a circular sampling polygon in Arena’s Map view.
When clicking on a point marker on the map, you will get a pop-up with the button. By clicking on this button, Arena opens a new web page with connection to Earth Map. First, you need to sign in and there are the following options:
With the last option, you can sign in without giving any information.
The same polygon submitted to EM looks as follows (with a query).
You can run GEE queries for your AOI by using the Statistics tools on the right side of the page.
You can get multitemporal results as shown in the following picture.

sections.title: Polygon data on the map view
sections.text:
Users can upload polygon (or point and line) layers to the map view: open the Add data menu and choose Upload KML, KMZ or Shapefile…, then select the file.
Arena’s map can show KML, KMZ, GeoJSON (.geojson or .json) or zipped Shapefile (.zip) files, up to 50 MB each, on top of the base map (or satellite image), as shown in the next images. After the upload, the map zooms to the content of the file. KML points without an icon style are shown with the default marker.
Uploaded files are listed in the Uploaded files group of the Layers tab: use the checkbox to show or hide a file, the slider below it to change its opacity and the × button to remove it. You can also upload several files into the Arena map view, if needed.
Note: the uploaded files are not stored anywhere. So, if you refresh the web browser window, all uploaded layers disappear. To share a map layer with the other users of the survey, add it as a WMS / WMTS service or XYZ tiles (see 9.7.5).

sections.title: WMS / WMTS services and XYZ tiles
Measuring distances and areas
sections.text:
Open the Tools menu and choose Measure distance or Measure area:
Click on the map to add points and double-click to finish. The measure bar at the top of the map shows the total distance (or the area and the perimeter); you can switch between Distance and Area and choose the Units (Automatic, meters, kilometers, square meters, hectares or square kilometers). Click Done (or press Esc) to end the measurement.

sections.title: Map screenshots
Areas of interest on the map
sections.text: The areas of interest defined in Survey info, Map tab (GeoJSON polygons used, for example, by the expression functions geoDistanceToAOIBoundary and geoAOIContaining) are available as layers in Data > Map, in the Areas of interest group of the Layers tab. Check an area to show it on the map, e.g., to see which plots fall inside it.

sections.title: Data export
sections.text:
Data of the current survey can be exported into a zip file that contains several CSV or Excel files. In the case of multicycle data, the selected cycle’s data will be exported or there is an option to export all data. The zip file contains all attributes grouped by entities. In the left side menu, select Data > Data Export. There are the following options for exporting data.
Options marked with an asterisk (*) are not compatible with data import: files exported with them cannot be imported back into Arena. Include result variables is shown only to users who can use the analysis, Include data from all cycles only in multi-cycle surveys and Include internal UUIDs only to system administrators.
You can also export data from Data Explorer (see 9.6.3) and the selected or filtered records from the records list.
Options: File format: Excel (.xlsx) / CSV (.csv) Include category items labels: for categorical data, export both code and label (2 columns). Include ancestor attributes: include the attributes of the parent entities, up to the root entity. Include files: include all files (e.g. images, documents) in a subfolder called "files". Include file attribute columns: add the file identifier and file name columns of file attributes. Include creation date: add the creation date of every entity (row) in a column called "date_created". Include categories: export the categories into a subfolder called "categories". Expand category items: add a Boolean column for every category item. Export single entities into separate files: otherwise their attributes are included in the nearest multiple ancestor entity. Include result variables: include the computed result variables from RStudio processing. Include data from all cycles: in a multi-cycle survey, export the data of all cycles. Include internal UUIDs: add the internal (database) identifiers in columns ending with "_uuid". Records modified after / Records modified before: export only the records modified after and/or before the given dates.
The next image shows an exported file containing forest inventory data.
The first column in each table is showing the cycle (‘record_cycle’).

sections.title: Data import
Importing data from CSV or Excel file (1/2)
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be provided as a .CSV (in Unicode, UTF-8; column separator is comma) or Excel file (.xlsx). Each file to be imported can contain data of one entity (or multiple attribute). In Excel files, cells with formulas, rich text or hyperlinks are read as plain values (the result of the formula, the text of the cell). The data import contains several steps.
STEP 1. Select the cycle
In case of a multicycle survey, the user has to select the target cycle (read more about cycles here).
STEP 2. Select Import Type gives two options as follows:
- Update existing records: select this method if the records are already entered and you can see them in the records list (Data → Records), but you need to add missing data under the root entity, or you need to update existing data.
- Insert new records: select this method if the survey is blank (i.e., no records yet), or the records to be imported are all new ones. Only the root level data can be imported as new records. All imported new records go into the Entry stage level.
For example, in the following survey "CLUSTER" is the root level entity, and a file to be imported should contain "cluster data" only.
STEP 3. Select entity
Select the target entity (or multiple attribute) to be updated from the hierarchy view under Import into multiple entity or attribute, by clicking on its name. With Insert new records, the root entity is selected automatically.
Click the link below the hierarchy view (Show names, Show labels and names, Show labels) to switch between labels, names, or labels and names:
(Default view)
With Update existing records, click Options to show the following options:
1) Allow/Prevent adding new entities, such as new sample plots into the database. [default: Allow] 2) Allow/Prevent updating records that are locked (i.e. in the Analysis stage). [default: Prevent] 3) Include files: import a .zip archive with the data file and the associated files (see Step 4b). 4) Delete selected entity's data in all records: all the instances of the selected entity, and their descendants, are deleted in all records before the new ones are inserted. Options 3 and 4 are available to system administrators only; option 4 is not available for the root entity.
STEP 4a. Select file
Click on this box to select a file to be imported, or drag and drop a file here:
It is recommended to use the data import (CSV/Excel) templates. Select the entity in the hierarchy view, then click Download template and choose CSV or Excel. Download all templates gets the templates of all the entities in a single file. Do not add other columns: for example, the label columns (e.g. land_use_label) of a data export are reported as invalid columns.
See in the next table information about data types to be imported:
Data type | Format
Numeric | Decimal separator is dot (.), for example 3.356
Integer
Text | CSV: A text that contains a comma should be in double quotes. E.g. "The plot falls into a lake, not accessed"
Boolean | true/false or 1/0
Categorical, Taxon | code (these are read in as texts). For key taxon attributes only the code column is required; the scientific and vernacular name columns are optional. Note: a vernacular name is always imported, if that is given in the input file.
Date | YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY.MM.DD, DD/MM/YYYY, DD.MM.YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY (e.g. 2025-03-20 or 20/03/2025)
Time | HH:MM (e.g. 10:35)
Coordinates | Use three columns: -attribute_name_srs: EPSG:CODE, for example EPSG:4326, or just an EPSG number -attribute_name_x: numeric -attribute_name_y: numeric
File | Use only one column: - attribute_name_file_name: the file name of the associated file (e.g. photo.jpg), exactly matching a file provided in the “files” subfolder inside the archive uploaded in Step 5 below. Leave the cell blank if no file applies to that record.
Multiple entry attributes | Import these as separate CSV/Excel tables, after importing the parent entity table

sections.title: Importing data from CSV or Excel file (2/2)
sections.text:
After selecting a file, the file can be validated in order to detect possible incompatibles with the target entity in the survey. The validation process only checks that the file contains valid data according to the data type of each attribute. Hence, this validation will not for example check that a numeric value is matching the (input) validation rule set for an attribute.
STEP 4b. Upload the associated files
If the entity being imported contains one or more file-type attributes (for example, a photo attached to a plot or tree record), the actual files are not embedded in the CSV/Excel file; the data file only carries the file name in the corresponding column, as shown in the Data Type table above.
To bring the files themselves into Arena together with the tabular data:
- Prepare a folder where you will put both the data file in tabular format (CSV/Excel file) and all the files referenced in the file-attribute column(s) of your data file;
- Copy the data file (.csv or .xlsx) inside the just prepared folder;
- Copy all the files referenced in the file-attribute column(s) of your CSV/Excel file into a subfolder called “files”; file names inside the archive must match exactly the file names listed in the CSV/Excel file (case-sensitive);
- Compress all the content of the folder (not the folder itself, but its content, that is the data file and the “files” subfolder) into a single .zip archive.
- In the import wizard, choose Update existing records, open Options and select Include files (system administrators only), then use the file upload box to select or drag and drop this .zip archive.
Arena stores each uploaded file against the correct record and file attribute automatically.
Previously imported files are replaced accordingly.
Tip Keep the total size of the .zip archive and of each individual file within Arena's general upload limits. For large photo sets, consider splitting the import into smaller batches by entity or by cycle.
Step 4c. Validate
After selecting the file, click Validate to detect possible incompatibilities with the target entity in the survey. The validation process checks that the file contains valid data according to the data type of each attribute, including, for file attributes, that every referenced file name is present in the uploaded archive.
It does not check, for example, that a numeric value satisfies the input validation rule set for that attribute.
When the validation finds errors, they are listed with the row number of the file and the error message. Click Export to download the list of errors.
STEP 5. Start import
Click on the button.
Confirm with Ok: the import cannot be rolled back. A progress bar shows the rows being processed, with the elapsed and remaining time; click Details to see the progress of each step.
When the import is complete, a summary shows the number of rows processed, records created and updated, entities created and deleted and values updated. If the import completes with errors, the errors are listed in the same way as in the validation, and they can be exported.

sections.title: Import data from Collect/Collect Mobile file
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .collect-data or .collect-backup format.
If a survey is created in OF Collect, and this survey is imported into Arena and published, data can also be imported into the Arena (later). This enables collection of data using OF Collect Mobile in data collection.
The checkbox "delete all records before import" means that all records (of the selected cycle) in the target survey will be deleted. Be cautious while using this selection!
Selection "Force import from another survey" allows users to import data from a collect-data file, which may have different survey name in Collect than in Arena, but the same schema (i.e. source and target schemas match).

sections.title: Import data from Arena/Arena Mobile file
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .zip format and earlier exported from Arena or Arena Mobile (in Arena: Data → Records, select the records, then Export → Export selected records (Arena format)). The survey structures must match between the target survey and in the file to be imported.
The conflict resolution strategy means that the user needs to decide what to do in a case where the same record, or a record with the same key attributes, is already in the database.
It contains three options:
- Skip if already existing: the record is skipped if it already exists in the database;
- Overwrite if updated: the existing record is overwritten with the imported data, if the imported record was modified more recently;
- Merge records: the data from the imported file will be attached to the existing record (see Merging data). By this means, for example a missing tree (entity) data can be imported into the records.
A record in the file matches an existing record when it has the same UUID or the same key attribute values, also when the keys are codes of large categories or taxonomies: in that case the records are merged (or skipped, or overwritten) instead of being duplicated. Merging records with the same keys but different UUIDs (e.g. records created with different Arena Mobile devices) can be disabled in the survey security settings (see Merging data).
The other options are:
- Ignore missing files: import the records even if some of the files they reference are not in the .zip file. Files already stored on the server do not need to be in the file again: Arena Mobile, for example, does not upload the files that the server already has.
- File upload chunk size: size of the parts in which the file is uploaded; use a smaller size with slow or unstable connections.
Select the file and click Generate preview. The Import preview shows, for each record in the file, its key attributes, the cycle, whether it already exists, the action that will be applied (Insert, Overwrite, Merge or Skip) and the modification dates of the existing and the imported record. Unselect the records you do not want to import, then click Import selected records and confirm. Records marked as Skip cannot be selected.
If you cancel the import while it is running, it stops after the record being processed. At the end, a summary shows the number of records processed, created, updated and skipped. Files with large records are imported quickly.

sections.title: Import data from ODK / ODK Collect
sections.text:
Data collected with ODK Collect can be imported into a published survey created from the same ODK form (see Chapter 5, Method 3). The file must be a .zip file with one folder per submission, each containing the submission.xml file and the media files of the submission (ODK Briefcase export).
In Data > Data Import, open the ODK / ODK Collect tab, select the cycle (if the survey has more than one), select the file and click Start import. Submissions already imported (with the same instance ID) are skipped: at the end, a summary shows the number of records created and of duplicate submissions skipped.

sections.title: Validation report
sections.text:
Errors in data can be detected by several means. While editing the data in Data Records, there can be an error message indicating that there is something wrong in the data. However, there is no easy way to find the erroneous data in the Data Records. So, for searching and browsing the erroneous data, we should use the Validation Report tool.
The data validation report is a table that is created by running through all data validation checks in the survey. It is essential to run this report and fix all errors in the data before the data enters the Analysis phase. Note: if your data are already at the Analysis step , you cannot edit the records. You need to submit the record back to Step 2.
In case of a multi-cycle dataset, the validation is executed for the selected cycle’s data only.
The validation report can look as follows:
The validation report shows all records that have issues, either ‘Warning’ or ‘Error’. The Error message will be automatically generated, if the custom "Error Message" is left blank in the survey designing phase.
The erroneous records can be directly accessed and edited from the Validation Report view.
Click a row (or its edit icon) to open the record. Click the arrows next to Path, Messages and Owner to sort the report. Use the buttons above the table to show only part of the messages:
- Filter attributes: show only the messages of the selected attributes.
- Filter messages: show only the selected message types (Required value, Invalid value, Duplicate value, Duplicate entity key, Duplicate record key, Node count, Custom validation).
- Filter records: show only the records matching an expression, written in JavaScript syntax as in Data Explorer (see 9.6.1), e.g. cluster_id <= 5.
The filters are also applied when exporting the report.
The validation report can be exported into an Excel file by clicking on the button. The report contains more information than the screen view, and it looks in MS Excel as follows.

sections.title: Merging data (1/2)
sections.text:
Records can be merged into one. This feature works only when it's applied to 2 records at a time.
Select the 2 records to merge in the records list (Data → Records), then press the Merge button on the top bar.
Merging data can be quite useful when, for example, data on the same site is collected using different devices; Arena and Arena Mobile don't allow creating records with the same identifiers (keys), but to make the data collection in the field faster, users can work on the same site (cluster) with different devices and combine the data later on. (e.g. when you have a survey with a structure cluster -> plot -> tree, users in the same cluster can collect tree data in different sample plots).
The survey must be prepared in a way that makes merging records easier.
During the merge process, the newer record will be considered as "source", while the older one as "target", so that values in the source record will go into the target record.
The merging process goes through every "entity" in the record, starting from the root.
- entities with the same key attribute values will be "merged";
- entities in the source record but not in the target one will be added;
- entities on the target record but not on the source one will be kept;
- attributes with values in the target record will not be replaced by values of the source record;
- empty attributes in the target record will be replaced with the ones in the source record;
A simple way to allow merging records is to start collecting data with one device, then on another device only the key attributes of the entities could be filled, and other attributes can be skipped/left blank. Here is an example of how 2 records will be merged; in this case, the survey has a quite simple structure such as cluster -> plot -> tree; the target record has 1 plot with 2 trees, the source record has a plot with the same ID as the target record and 1 tree with an ID different from the ones of the trees in the target record plot; the expected result is to have the "new" tree inside the target record plot, like this:
Target record | Source record | Merged record
Cluster: Cluster ID: 1a Region: R1 District: R1a Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S1 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S2 | Cluster: Cluster ID: 1b Region: District: Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 3 Tree species: S3 | Cluster: Cluster ID: 1a Region: R1 District: R1a Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S1 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S2 Tree [3]: Tree ID: 3 Tree species: S3
In case the source record contains another plot, with an ID different from the one of the plots already in the target record, also the "new" plot will be added to the target record, like in this example:
Target record | Source record | Merged record
Cluster: Cluster ID: 1a Region: R1 District: R1a Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S1 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S2 | Cluster: Cluster ID: 1b Region: District: Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 3 Tree species: S3 Plot [2]: Plot ID: 2 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S2 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S4 | Cluster: Cluster ID: 1a Region: R1 District: R1a Plot [1]: Plot ID: 1 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S1 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S2 Tree [3]: Tree ID: 3 Tree species: S3 Plot [2]: Plot ID: 2 Tree [1]: Tree ID: 1 Tree species: S2 Tree [2]: Tree ID: 2 Tree species: S4
Before applying for the merge, a preview of the results will be shown and the user will have to confirm the merge; once confirmed, the "source" record will be deleted and will no longer be accessible, while the target record will be modified, adding value from the source record.
When 2 records have too many differences from each other, a warning message will be shown to the user; in that case, the user could have selected 2 records that are not compatible for the merge.
Merging records with the same keys

sections.title: Merging data (2/2)
sections.text:
Records with the same key attribute values can come from different Arena Mobile devices, or from Arena files imported with the Merge records conflict resolution strategy. When they are uploaded or imported with the merge option, they are merged into the existing record instead of being duplicated (merging follows the rules described above).
This is allowed by default. To prevent it, go to Home → Survey Info → Security, unselect Allow merging records with same keys (e.g. records created in different Arena Mobile devices) and click Save. When the option is not selected, importing a record with the same keys as an existing one stops with an error.

sections.title: Exporting a printable document
sections.text:
To export a printable document of a record, follow the next steps:
- Open a record in Data → Records.
- Navigate to the page you want to print. This is only needed when printing the current page.
- Click the PDF icon (Export Document) in the record header bar.
- In the "Export printable document" dialog, select the options and click Download.
Option | Explanation
Format | PDF or Word (.docx). The Word file can be edited further before printing.
Content | Full survey: the whole record, with the survey label and description as the title. Current page only: only the entity instance currently shown in the form (e.g. the plot or tree you are viewing), with the entity label as the title. Its subpages are not included.
Include QR code | Adds a QR code to the first page. Available only with "Current page only".
Page orientation | Portrait or Landscape. The selection will be the document default. Entities with their own orientation set in the Print tab override it.
The document is generated in the language currently selected in the form's language selector, and for the cycle of the record. The downloaded file is named after the survey, the cycle and, for "Current page only", the entity label.
Note: "Current page only" requires a specific entity instance to be open. If the current page belongs to a multiple entity and no row or form is selected, the dialog shows a message. In that case, navigate to a specific instance or export the full survey.
What is included in the document
- The layout follows the Form Designer. Attributes are placed according to the form grid (columns and positions). Multiple entities displayed as tables are printed as tables. Multiple entities displayed as forms are printed once per instance, each under its own heading.
- Entities on their own page, and multiple entities at the upper levels of the hierarchy, start on a new page.
- Code attributes show the item label. Taxon attributes show the scientific name followed by the code.
- Boolean attributes use the label value set in the attribute (Yes/No or True/False).
- Image file attributes are printed as pictures. Other file types show the file name.
- Attributes set as Hide in entry form, and nodes that are not relevant or not visible in the record, are not printed.
- Calculated result attributes from processing chains are not included.
Example of a printed page (current page only, with QR code):

sections.title: QR code
sections.text:
When the "Include QR code" option is enabled, Arena stores a read-only PDF copy of the exported page on the server and prints a QR code in the top-right corner of the first page. Scanning the QR code with any smartphone opens the stored PDF.
- The link is valid for one year.
- Exporting the same page again with the QR code option updates the stored PDF with the current data and extends the validity by another year. The QR code and its link remain unchanged, ensuring that previously printed copies continue to work.
- The QR link can be accessed without logging in to Arena. Anyone who has the printed document can view that page's data. Therefore, carefully consider whether to use this feature for records containing personal, confidential, or otherwise sensitive information.

sections.title: Creating a processing chain (1/2)
sections.text:
Data processing in Arena is implemented using R scripts. Each survey has its own set of scripts, which can be created and modified by the Survey Administrator or Data Analyst. The processing can be executed either in a cloud-based RStudio environment or locally using R and RStudio installed on a personal computer, which is the recommended approach.
Data processing is carried out through a calculation chain consisting of the result variables to be calculated. Each computation within the chain is referred to in this manual as a calculation step. While a survey can contain several calculation chains, only one chain can be designated for applying the Sampling Design and Statistical Analysis methods.
Advantages of the processing chain
- Automated calculation result attributes (e.g., tree volume, biomass, carbon),
- One script – it is transparent and easy to repeat,
- R provides powerful statistical engine,
- Efficiency and reproducibility of inventory workflows by standardizing processing steps,
- Provides a foundation for reporting and documentation.
The concept of using a data processing chain in sampling-based assessment is illustrated in the following chart.
Chains are common across all cycles. If the user needs to apply different data processing rules by cycles, this needs to be taken into account inside the R scripts.
Start creating a new calculation chain by clicking button.
Then give the calculation chain information.
Input fields
- Processing chain label * name for the chain (required),
- Description * descriptive text about the chain (optional),
- Sampling Design * enable if you have sampling-based data (only one chain per survey); the Sampling Design tab is then shown,
- Records * number of records on different steps (of the selected cycle)
By default, the form of an existing processing chain is locked (a chain you have just created stays unlocked). Use these two buttons to unlock/lock the form.
RStudio options (expand the RStudio panel of the Basic tab)
1) If enabled, only the analysis stage data will be copied to the RStudio session. 2) Only selected records’ data are submitted to the RStudio session. 3) Enable this option if the result variables are read back into the Arena server from the RStudio session with [system/persist-results.R]
A chain must contain at least one calculation step, represented by a result variable. You can add either a quantitative (numeric) variable or a categorical (coded) variable.
For example, tree stem volume is a quantitative variable.
First, click the button.
Then, select the entity name from the dropdown list.
Then fill in the variable’s name, label (optional), unit (optional), and number of decimal digits (optional, used in Data Explorer only). The variable names must be unique in a survey.
Select if you want to compute area-based results for the given variable, such as "volume per hectare" or "number of trees per hectare". In the Statistical Analysis with a Shiny app, we can only report the area-based variables.
IMPORTANT: Follow these steps while renaming an area-based result variable 1) disable "area-based estimate" and approve to delete the node, 2) rename your result variable, and 3) enable back active again
R scripts can only be created and edited in RStudio. In Arena, they can be viewed but not modified. Click Save & Back to return to the previous screen.
You will see the list of results variables as follows.
Note 1: In the label text, the suffix (C) means that this is a calculated (chain) attribute.
Note 2: After saving a result variable, its properties can be edited but the parent entity cannot be changed.
Note 3: When you edit an existing result variable, use the arrow buttons at the bottom of the page to move to the previous or next result variable of the chain, Back to return to the chain, and Delete to delete the variable.
ACTIVE/DEACTIVATE variable button: This method allows users to include or exclude a result variable in the data processing in R.

sections.title: Creating a processing chain (2/2)
sections.text:
Note: if you have earlier processed your results with an "area-based" result variable that you want to deactivate, the results per hectare ("_ha") will still emerge in the Data Explorer and in the CSV/Excel export data. If you want to remove this "per hectare" attribute, first deselect "area-based estimate" in the attribute’s properties page, and then deactivate that attribute. Then run the analysis chain one more time in RStudio.
Categorical result variables are used for data aggregation and reporting. Click the button to add a new categorical result variable.
Select the entity, then fill in the name and label (optional). The categorical variable needs to be linked with an existing (flat) category: select it in the Category dropdown list, as in the example below. Next to the list:
- Add creates a new category and links it to the variable,
- Edit opens the selected category,
- Manage opens the list of the categories of the survey.
Then click Save & Back.
IMPORTANT: When using a computed categorical attribute, ensure that the R script does not return NA values from RStudio to the Arena server, as this may cause issues when reading JSON data. To avoid this, create a default category, such as "No Data" or "Other", and assign all missing values to that category (for example, code 0). e.g. plot$plot_elevation_class[ is.na( plot$plot_elevation_class)] <- ‘0’
The calculation chain now looks as follows.
Note: Some computed variables may depend on the results of previous calculations. For example, above-ground biomass must be computed before below-ground biomass. The order of variables can be adjusted by clicking and dragging the handle icon next to the variable name and dropping it in the desired location.
Note: If the window gets "frozen" while moving the variables (as below), refresh your browser.
If an entity contains a result variable but no associated data, it will not be included in the processing performed in RStudio. In such cases, a warning icon will be displayed, as shown in the image below.
After all result variables have been added, the survey must be published before they can be used. Click.

sections.title: RStudio in programming and data processing (1/3)
sections.text:
R scripts can be created, debugged, and run in RStudio. An overview of the entire processing chain is provided in the following figure.
The following two options are available for using RStudio with Arena:
- Use RStudio Server in the cloud, or
- Use locally installed RStudio (in your machine).
To run RStudio locally, ensure that:
- R version 4.1.3 or newer is installed.
- The rstudioapi package is installed.
- An active internet connection is available.
- You start a new RStudio session.
The workflow for both RStudio options is as follows:
- Publish the survey. This step is required whenever changes have been made to the survey structure, survey data, or calculation chain.
- Select whether you want to submit all data or only analysis step data to RStudio.
Note: For multi-cycle surveys, only the data from the currently selected cycle will be submitted to RStudio.
- Click the RStudio Remote (RStudio Server) or RStudio Local button in the RStudio panel to start the process. Note: The RStudio process cannot be started if no data are available for submission (i.e. all record counts are zero).
- The following message will be displayed. The message differs slightly depending on whether you are using the server-based or local RStudio environment:
Click OK to continue.
Arena will automatically copy the initialization script to your clipboard .
- RStudio Server: RStudio will open automatically.
Local RStudio: Start RStudio on your computer.
- Paste the copied script into the RStudio Console (Ctrl+V) and execute it. This step uploads all survey scripts from Arena's PostgreSQL database to RStudio.
- In the Files pane, the following structure will be available
arena.R = Main program file (do not edit!). system/ = Directory containing system-generated files (do not edit!). sampling/ = Directory containing scripts for base-unit weights and plot areas (can be edited). user/ = Directory containing scripts for result variables, one file per variable numbered in chain order, e.g. user/001-tree-tree_volume.R (can be edited).
- The startup script automatically opens the arena.R file. Run the first two lines of the script to initialize the session.
The file system/init.R contains system initialization commands, including database connection and configuration settings. When using RStudio Server, the initialization process installs a large number of R packages required by Arena into the current RStudio session. In Local RStudio, only a small set of essential packages is installed, and only if they are not already available .
The complete list of packages used by Arena can be found in: system/init/init-packages.R
Initialization typically takes a few seconds when a new RStudio session is started. Subsequent executions within the same environment are usually faster because the required packages and settings have already been configured.
If there is this error in the R Console: or some package is not loaded, as in the following case simply run system/init.R again! This error is caused by R or RStudio.
system/login.R displays two input dialogs to authenticate access to the Arena database. First, enter your Arena username (email address), and then enter your password. For security reasons, the password is masked and displayed as asterisks.
After a successful login, a confirmation message similar to the following will appear in the R Console: "User myusername@x.org successfully logged in"
- Run the third line of the script:.
source('system/read-data.R')
This script initializes the survey data objects as R data frames and downloads the data from Arena. The loaded objects can be viewed in the Environment pane in RStudio. The following data will be added into the R project:
- Data from all entities included in the calculation chain.
- Data from the Base Unit and Clustering entities.
- All categorical and taxonomic tables, stored as lists of data frames.
- The schema summary table (arena.schemaSummary).

sections.title: RStudio in programming and data processing (2/3)
sections.text:
- The chain summary object (arena.chainSummary), which contains information about the structure and content of the calculation chain.
- Once the data have been loaded successfully, open the user/ folder to access the scripts associated with the survey's result variables.
This folder contains the common file for adding R scripts (as functions) that are common for all calculation steps following file 000-common.R
Important: about using R packages Whenever possible, load all your required packages in 000-common.R, as this provides a single location for managing package dependencies and simplifies script maintenance. Note that RStudio Server runs on a Linux environment. As a result, some R packages that are available on other operating systems may not work on the server. When using additional packages, avoid loading them with the library() function. Instead, use the usePackage() function, for example: usePackage("lmfor") The usePackage() function checks whether the specified package is already installed. If the package is not available, it is installed automatically. The function is defined in the system file init-packages.R: Since a large number of packages may be loaded during an RStudio session, it is recommended to explicitly qualify function names with their package names to avoid conflicts. For example: dplyr::select(), dplyr::filter() This practice improves code readability and helps ensure that the intended function is used when multiple packages provide functions with the same name.
- The scripts located in the user/ and sampling/ folders are the primary files that require user-developed code.
Within the RStudio project, survey data are organized into data frames corresponding to each entity. In addition, two lists of data frames are available: categories and taxonomies. For example, if the survey includes a code list named land_use, it can be accessed as categories$land_use.
Taxonomic tables may also contain additional attributes, such as species-specific wood density values. Since these attributes are stored as character fields in Arena, they must be converted to numeric data types before being used in calculations.
- Once all scripts have been tested, saved, and executed without errors, run the main program by opening arena.R and clicking the Source button.
This process uploads all updated R scripts and writes the computed results back to the Arena database. If the calculation chain includes Sampling Design and Statistical Analysis settings, the resulting output tables will also be exported as CSV files (see Chapter 10.4.4 for details).
- RStudio Server users: After the processing has completed successfully, close your RStudio session: in Arena, open Analysis > RStudio sessions in the left side panel and click Terminate.
Terminating the connection frees server resources and makes them available to other users of the cloud-based RStudio service.
If RStudio Server does not start
If you encounter an error message like the one shown below in your web browser, it indicates that the RStudio Server instance is currently unable to start.
In such cases, please wait 5 to 10 minutes and try again. This issue may occur when many users are attempting to access the system simultaneously, resulting in limited server resources.
Working with external files (e.g. CSVs and image files)
If you are using RStudio Server and need to create or save files during your session, such as CSV files, images, or other outputs, please refer to Annex 3 for detailed instructions.
Error handling
In arena.R, each module invocation within the processing chain includes an argument for capturing and handling errors, as illustrated in the example below.

sections.title: RStudio in programming and data processing (3/3)
sections.text:
All errors encountered during script execution are collected in a global error log. This log is evaluated by the script system/persist-user-scripts.R when user-developed R scripts are saved back to the Arena server. If any errors are present in the log, execution of the calculation chain is halted and a warning message is displayed in the R Console. All reported errors must be resolved before the chain can be executed successfully.
After fixing the erroneous R code, the error log must be cleared before rerunning the scripts. There are three ways to do this:
- Restart the chain from system/init.R. This clears the error log automatically. However, the survey data needs to be reloaded from the Arena server into RStudio, which may take considerable time for large datasets.
- Run cleanGlobalErrors() in the R Console. After clearing the error log, rerun the chain starting from the corrected script or module.
- Add cleanGlobalErrors() to 000-common.R. By including this command in 000-common.R, the error log will be cleared automatically when you rerun the chain from that point.
Choosing the second or third option is often more efficient, as it avoids reloading data from the server and reduces processing time during script development and testing.
Problems with system/persist-results.R
IIn some cases, computed results cannot be written back to the Arena database. One common cause is the presence of one or more data frame columns that contain only NA values. When this occurs, error messages similar to the examples below may be displayed.
Or the error message is this one:
The first step is to inspect the result variables and verify whether any of them contain only NA values. If all result variables appear valid, the issue may originate from the input data retrieved from Arena.
A practical solution is to remove any columns that consist entirely of missing values before rerunning the result persistence process. For example, if the error occurs in the tree data frame, the following command removes all columns whose values are exclusively NA:
tree[sapply(tree, function(x) all(is.na(x)))] <- NULL
After removing the affected columns, rerun the system/persist-results.R script to write the results back to the Arena database.
Viewing updated scripts in Arena
User scripts are saved back to the Arena database by the system/persist-user-scripts.R script.
If an updated script is not immediately visible in the Arena script editor, refresh your web browser to reload the latest version from the database.

sections.title: About computing area-based variables
sections.text:
In most forest inventory projects, results are typically reported by area units. In contrast, area-based estimates are generally not required for activities such as interviews and socio-economic surveys.
When you create a result variable and enable the Area-based estimate option, Arena automatically creates a corresponding variable in the database (for example, tree_volume becomes tree_volume_ha).
In Arena, all variables generated by the processing chain can be displayed by enabling .
In the RStudio project, a new sampling folder is created containing additional files used for sampling-based estimation, as described in the following sections.
The sampling/ folder contains scripts for calculating base-unit weights and the sampling areas required for area-based result variables.
Depending on the survey design, base-unit weights can be defined in different ways. For example, all sample plots may be assigned equal weights, while inaccessible plots can be assigned a weight of zero and excluded from the estimation process.

After the full processing chain has been executed successfully in RStudio, all user-developed scripts are saved back to the Arena server. If the “Results Read Back from RStudio” option is enabled, the computed result variables are also written back to the Arena database.
These result variables can then be viewed, explored, and aggregated using the Arena Explorer tool. The figure below illustrates how area-based result variables are displayed in both the Explorer view and the Hierarchy view.
Variables marked with (C) are computed variables, indicating that their values are generated through the calculation chain rather than entered directly by users’ input data.
Weight and plot area attributes
When the chain has a base unit (see the Sampling Design tab), Arena creates the following sampling attributes every time you publish the survey:
- weight, in the base unit entity (default script: plot$weight <- 1);
- <entity>_plot_area_ (e.g. tree_plot_area_), in every entity with an active area-based result variable of the chain (default script: tree$tree_plot_area_ <- NA: replace NA with the plot area formula).
These decimal attributes are not shown in the data entry forms and cannot be deactivated. Arena deletes them when they are no longer needed, for example when the base unit changes or an entity has no active area-based result variables anymore. Their scripts are in the sampling/ folder of the RStudio project (the weight first). To see them in the list of result variables, select Show sampling attributes:

sections.title: Sampling strategy
sections.text:
This section will cover defining a sample strategy in Arena. A sample strategy is the combination of sample design along with an estimator (formula) from which is calculated an estimate for a parameter of interest. For many strategies the sample design and formula are so closely associated that the term "design" is used when "strategy" is meant, we will follow this convention.
Arena supports the following sampling strategies: 1) simple random sampling and systematic sampling; 2) stratified sampling; and 3) single stage or cluster sampling. In addition, the script can compute area estimates for 4) two-phase sampling (UNDER DEVELOPMENT, non-clustered, or clustered).
Definitions and Background
Most forest inventory measurement protocols use a set of circles or rectangles; the set is arranged geometrically around the sample point for the set, see figure below.
In a majority of inventories, the set is referred to as a cluster and individual elements are referred to as plots. One exception is the Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) program of the United States Forest Service, which refers to the set as a plot and individual elements as subplots. To avoid confusion between the two uses of "plot" we will refer to the FIA set as the FIA-plot.
In Open Foris Calc, the smallest unit of measured area is called a base unit, and it is assumed that the base unit is of a single stand type. For many inventories the plot is the base unit. Although in some inventories the plot can be mapped into different stand types. One example of this is FIA, which has the field crews divide the subplots into different stands if there is a stand boundary which can be repeatable mapped.
Typically, trees are measured on clusters of plots, where the plots may vary in size and/or number depending on the diameter class of the tree. Therefore, each entity that contains "area-based" variable(s) gets a new result attribute automatically in a processing chain, for example "tree" gets attribute "tree_plot_area_".

sections.title: Settings for sampling design (1/2)
sections.text:
The Sampling Design tab, shown once the Sampling Design option is selected in the Basic tab, contains a form for a description of the survey strategy. The form looks as follows:
The content is as follows:
Line | Required? | Explanation
Sampling strategy | Optional If NONE, statistical analysis is not executed | Options: 0. none 1. random sampling 2. systematic sampling 3. stratified random sampling 4. stratified systematic sampling 5. two-phase sampling
Base unit | Yes | The smallest unit of measured area
Stratum attribute | Yes, if stratified sampling strategy | Select a categorical attribute (base unit or its parent level). Only one attribute can be selected. This can also be a categorical result attribute. Areas of strata should be given in.
Clustering entity (within cluster sampling) | Optional | Set the clustering entity. In cluster sampling, results are aggregated first at the base unit level, then at the cluster level, and then at the domain level (strata / reporting unit). if blank: a single stage survey.
Clustering only for variances? | Optional | As a single stage survey: A clustering entity is set, but clusters are only applied for computing variances, but not for means.
Non-response bias correction? | Optional | If enabled, calculation requires a category table 'sampling_units_plan' containing the sampling design (i.e. planned number of samples, and clusters if clustered sampling). See more information below.
Total reporting area (ha) | Optional | Non-stratified sampling case. Area of interest for reporting "totals".
The two-phase sampling strategy contains more selections, as follows.
Base unit, Stratum attribute, and Clustering entity are explained in the previous table. In two-phase sampling, the stratum attribute is used to sub-stratify the first-phase sample: only attributes whose name is also a column of the 1st phase category are listed. The additional required information is as follows.
1st phase category | Category table name, that contains the 1st phase samples.
Join entity (2nd phase) | 2nd phase entity (table) to be joined with 1st phase table.
Join by using Sampling Point Data linkage? | YES: 2nd phase entity (‘plot’ in the image above) is getting its key attribute values from the 1st phase category table (sampling_point_data). NO: 2nd phase entity (‘plot’ in the image above) is not linked with the 1st phase category table. The following two questions will arise.
Join attribute (1st phase) | Column name in the 1st phase category table
Join attribute (2nd phase) | Attribute name in the 2nd phase entity (table). This can be categorical or text data type only.
All selections in the "Sampling Design" will be submitted as a JSON file into the R project, and they will be available as a named list arena.chainSummary in RStudio.
The JSON chain summary file can be downloaded from the Advanced functions menu of the chain with the command.
Read more about the Arena JSON file in Annex 5.
Areas of strata
Stratified sampling requires computation of inclusion probabilities by stratum. In Arena, inclusion probabilities are expressed as "expansion factors" (which are equal to the inverse of inclusion probability).
There are two methods in Arena script to compute expansion factor for a base unit:
- Computation with the help of sample weights in stratum, i.e. Exp_factor = [base unit weight in stratum] / (sum([base unit weights in stratum])
- Areas of stratum is known, i.e. Exp_factor = [area in stratum] / (sum([base unit weights in stratum])
Method A does not allow you to compute "Totals" (such as total volume, biomass) correctly. However, per hectare results can be computed.
In case B, sampling areas must be provided. These are given via the category table of the stratification entity, in a column named "area". All areas are given in hectares (or acres). The total inventory area is the sum of the column "area". The content of the ‘reporting table’ is described next.
