sections.title: Area for statistical analysis
sections.text:
If the extent of samples is known (such as sampling plot areas in forest inventories), Arena’s script can always compute results per hectare basis, such as tree volume per hectare. For computing the "total" results for a given area of interest (AOI), such as total tree volume, the user must give in the area. The method of giving the AOI (extent) depends on the sampling strategy, as follows:
- Non-stratified sampling. In the Sampling Design tab, enter the area in the Total reporting area (ha) field:
- Stratified sampling, total AOI is known but the areas of strata are not known in advance: Same as in Case #1. Areas of strata are computed according to proportion of strata (i.e. sum of weights in stratum divided by the total sum of weights across all strata).
- Stratified sampling, the areas of strata are known in advance: Areas (ha) are given within the attribute’s category table as an "extra property", as follows:
- AOI (extent) is not known, or it is not relevant: the script assumes the reporting area is equal to 100 ha.

sections.title: Non-response bias corrections
sections.text:
A problem common to nearly all sample-based surveys is partial or complete non-response from some of the selected sample units. Arena script can apply the Weighting Class Adjustment method and compute weight adjustment factors based on data about the planned number of sampling units. In this case, missing observations are ignored and an adjustment factor is incorporated into a sample weight to compensate for non-response or situations where all or part of a sample (plot) falls outside the population.
The weight adjustment requires information about the planned number of Primary Sampling Units (PSUs) and Secondary Sampling Units (SSUs).
In a forest inventory, Primary Sampling Units can be sample plots or clusters, by strata in case of stratified sampling. Secondary Sampling Units can be sample plots.
In stratified sampling, the number of PSUs and SSUs are given within the stratum attribute’s category table, as follows:
In the example above, the area of Stratum 1 is 30 ha, and the initial number of clusters (PSUs) is 85, and the number of sample plots in a cluster is 4.
In the next example, the non-response bias correction is not computed for missing clusters, but only for missing sample plots (SSUs):
And in the next example, the non-response bias correction is computed only for missing clusters (PSUs) in strata, but not for sample plots (SSUs):
If this lookup table is missing or its format is incorrect, Arena’s R script cannot compute corrections.
Stratified sampling case:
level_1_code: stratified, give the stratum attributes’ codes (text) label_en: Label (text) area: stratum area (in hectares. Optional) design_psu: planned number of primary samples (such as clusters) in strata (numeric) design_ssu: planned number of samples (such as plots) in clusters (numeric)
NOTE: This part of the Arena platform and R scripts will be further developed by the OF Arena Team and changes will be documented in this manual and the GitHub repository.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (1/2)
sections.text:
Arenalytics is an analytical dashboard developed for reporting and exploring data collected and processed with Open Foris Arena. It was designed to address one of the main challenges of sample-based assessments: generating reliable statistics, tables, and figures from large and complex survey datasets without requiring users to predefine all reporting outputs in advance. The dashboard was developed particularly for forest inventories and other sample-based assessments where users need to produce estimates such as biomass, tree density, volume, carbon stocks, or other indicators across multiple reporting domains. The dashboard allows users to dynamically analyse survey results by selecting measures, dimensions, and filters, producing estimates, totals, means, and reliability statistics on demand.
The Arenalytics workflow begins in Open Foris Arena, where survey data are collected and processed using a calculation chain. Once the processing chain has been executed in RStudio, Arena automatically generates Minimum Area Unit (MAU) files that contain pre-computed result variables and supporting attributes required for reporting. These files are packaged into a ZIP archive and loaded into Arenalytics for analysis.
After loading a MAU zip file, Arenalytics performs automatic validation checks and provides a survey summary to help users verify that the uploaded data are ready for analysis. Users can then select an entity, choose one or more measures to analyse, and define dimensions and filters that determine how results will be aggregated and presented. Dimensions can originate from either the original survey data or from the processing chain, enabling flexible reporting across administrative units, forest types, diameter classes, species groups, and many other categories. The resulting tables are generated instantly and updated whenever the settings in the ‘Cross outputs settings’ section change.
Workflow Summary: Arena Survey with Data and Processing Chain → Run Chain in RStudio → Generate MAU ZIP file → Load data into Arenalytics → Select Entity and Dimensions → Click Run analysis → Select Measures and Filters → Review & Export results → Create figures → Generate reports
The dashboard can be accessed through a web application or installed locally from its open-source R package, making it suitable for both online and offline environments:
- Use the online version. Open the hosted dashboard in your web browser: https://openforis-shiny.shinyapps.io/arenalytics/
- RECOMMENDED: Install and run locally in a Rstudio instance with
if (!require(remotes)) install.packages("remotes")
if (!require(arenalytics)) remotes::install_github("openforis/arenalytics", upgrade="never")
arenalytics::shiny_run_arenalytics()
The internal showcase presentation also notes that a demo dataset is available in the About section of the application. A step-by-step guideline to Arenalytics is available here.
The outcome of the Arena processing chain is a ZIP file of semi-aggregated data that will serve as input for Arenalytics, a Minimum Area Unit (MAU) file. The MAU file contains data aggregated to the Minimum Area Unit level, which is defined as the smallest homogeneous land unit in the survey area. In the Arena processing chain, the MAU is equivalent to the base unit used for statistical estimation.
Examples:
- If a plot is completely homogeneous (single land use or vegetation type), the plot itself is the MAU.
- If a plot is divided into several land-use or vegetation sections, then each homogeneous section becomes a separate MAU unit. Estimation variables are first computed for these sections and then aggregated to higher reporting levels.
The MAU file is automatically generated by an Arena system script as a ZIP file. It contains:
- Result estimates for each base unit (MAU).
- All relevant dimensions derived from categorical, taxonomic, and Boolean attributes.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (2/2)
sections.text:
- Pre-computed measures that Arenalytics can subsequently aggregate into tables, charts, means, totals, and sampling-error estimates for any user-selected combination of dimensions.
Arenalytics reads measures at the MAU level and dynamically aggregates them to any reporting level (forest type, species, administrative region, diameter class, etc.) requested by the user. For a typical forest inventory case, where plots may be split into land-use strata or forest types, you can think of the MAU file as a dataset where each record represents one homogeneous plot section together with all its computed area-based variables and reporting dimensions.
The generated MAU ZIP file can be stored on the Arena server to facilitate archiving and future retrieval. Follow these steps:
- Unlock the chain
- Click Advanced functions and then Upload MAU.zip
- Once the file is uploaded, you will see an option to download or delete this file:
The MAU.zip file is linked to the cycle selected in the header: if the survey has more than one cycle, Arena asks you to confirm the cycle before uploading the file, and Download MAU.zip and Delete MAU.zip work on the file of the current cycle.
Only .zip files are accepted. If a MAU.zip file has already been uploaded for the chain, Arena asks you to confirm before replacing it. Upload MAU.zip and Delete MAU.zip are available only when the chain is unlocked, Download MAU.zip also when it is locked.

sections.title: Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text: This chapter explains how to copy an existing processing chain with R scripts from one survey into another without rebuilding a new chain step by step.

sections.title: Overview
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey

sections.title: Prerequisites
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
- You must have Survey Administrator or Data Analyst permissions in the destination survey (the one you want to copy the chain into).
- You must also have access to the source survey (the one the chain is copied from). Only surveys you can access, and that already contain at least one chain, are offered as a source.
- The destination survey should already contain the entities that the source chain's calculated variables refer to (for example, plot or tree), using the same entity names. Arena checks this for you before the clone runs; if the entities do not exist in the target survey, the analysis variables associated to those entities won’t be cloned.

sections.title: Step-by-step: cloning a chain
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
- Open the destination survey (the survey you want the chain copied into) and go to Analysis → Chains.
- In the Chains panel, click the button “Clone from another survey”.
- In the Clone chain from another survey dialog, select the Source survey (or template) from the dropdown list. Only surveys and templates you have access to, and that contain at least one chain, appear here.
- Select the Source chain you want to copy from the list of chains available in that survey.
- Arena automatically runs a compatibility check, comparing the entities used by the source chain's calculation steps with the entities available in the destination survey.
- Review the compatibility results. If everything is compatible, confirm the clone by clicking Clone. Entities that do not exist in the destination survey are marked as missing in target survey: select Skip analysis attributes for entities missing in the target survey to clone the chain without their analysis attributes (otherwise Clone stays disabled).
- Arena creates the new chain in the destination survey, copies the scripts and calculated variables, and then opens the newly created chain automatically so you can review it.

sections.title: What happens after cloning
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
- A new chain is created in the destination survey with a new, unique identifier, it is entirely separate from the source chain.
- All R scripts from the source chain are copied over as-is; you can edit them afterwards like any other chain script.
- Calculated variables are re-created under the matching entities of the destination survey, together with any categories or taxonomies they depend on.
- The new chain is validated automatically once created, and any issues (for example, an expression referencing an attribute that does not exist in the destination survey) are flagged for you to resolve, the same way validation works for a chain you build manually.
- You are taken directly to the newly created chain, ready for review, adjustment, and publishing.

sections.title: Notes and limitations
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
- Cloning copies the chain definition and scripts; it does not copy previously computed results or published data — you still need to run the chain in RStudio to generate results in the destination survey.
- Only chains you can access (i.e., chains belonging to surveys you are a member of, or to published templates) can be used as a source.
- If the source and destination surveys use different names for otherwise equivalent entities, rename the entity in one of the two surveys first so the compatibility check can match them.
- A survey can contain more than one chain; cloning adds a new chain alongside any chains that already exist in the destination survey; it does not replace them.
- When you clone a whole survey (Clone in the new survey page), its chains are cloned too.

sections.title: Deleting a chain
sections.text: A calculation chain can be deleted from the Advanced functions menu. Unlock the form and click Delete chain. This action cannot be canceled.

sections.title: User roles and invitation to access a survey
User roles
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
Each survey is hosted by one or more Survey Administrators. A Survey Administrator can invite new users by sending an email invitation from Arena.
A Survey Manager status is a user privilege and not a role: this user can create a new survey and become a Survey Administrator for that new survey.
To become a Survey Manager and start creating a new survey, please go to www.openforis-arena.org and click on the Create an account link, under the Login button:
Note: User roles like- “Data Analyst”, “Data Cleanser” and “Data Editor” can be provided only when the survey is published. During the survey designing phase only “Survey Administrator” role can be provided to another Arena user. Unpublishing an already published survey does not remove the assigned user roles from the survey. Field crews or field data collectors are generally provided access with the “Data Editor” role in the survey.
Fill in the form. It is recommended to start using a template, read more about them in this Annex. Then send the request and wait for approval. You will receive an email with the details on how to access Arena.
The users are divided into the following roles, each of them having different access rights to the tools, surveys and data.
Permission | Survey Administrator | Data Analyst | Data Cleanser | Data Editor | Guest

Notes on the table above:
- The Dashboard, the Data Explorer and the Validation report are available to Survey Administrators, Data Analysts and Data Cleansers. They are not available to Data Editors.
- The Map is available to Survey Administrators and Data Analysts.
- Data import is possible only in published surveys.
- System administrators have all the permissions in all the surveys of the server.
- Guest: can view and export the records of the survey, also in Arena Mobile, but cannot add, edit, delete or submit them. Like the other data roles, it can be assigned only when the survey is published. Add the guest to a user group with qualifiers to show only the records of that group (see 11.3).

sections.title: Invitation to survey
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A Survey Administrator can invite new users to get access to the current published survey.
To send an invitation to a new survey user or a group of users, go to the section and click the button. The following form will appear.
The invitation is sent to all set email addresses. Fill in first the email addresses (type each address and press Add), then select a Role, and type an additional message, if needed. The Permissions of the selected role are shown below it. Only system administrators see the System administrator checkbox, used to invite other system administrators.
This is an example of email that the client will get:
The text of the message is shorter if the invited person (i.e. email) is already a registered Arena user.
If a recipient does not get an email, the message might be blocked by a strict firewall filter on the recipient’s end. Ask the recipient to check their spam, junk, and clutter folder for the invitation message. A user invitation will be deleted if it is not accepted in 1 month. If the invited user is currently logged in the Arena platform, then this user might need to log out and log in again in order to see the survey properly.

sections.title: User Grouping
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey

sections.title: Overview
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A Survey Administrator can organize the people who collect data for a survey into named groups (e.g., by region, team, or organization). A group can optionally carry one or more qualifiers (key/value pairs that automatically restrict and pre-fill the data that its members collect) so that each group only can see and edit the records that belong to them.
User Groups are useful when:
- Several field teams share the same survey but should not see or edit each other’s records.
- Records must be automatically tagged with a region, project, or organization code as soon as they are created, based on who is entering the data.
- You want to get a quick overview of which users are assigned to which team, and a method to reassign them.

sections.title: Accessing User Groups
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
Only users with a Survey Administrator role in the current survey can create, edit, delete groups, or manage members.
User Groups are managed per survey, via the Users section of the survey menu:
- Select the survey and go to Users on the left-hand side menu.
- Select the User Groups tab.
The User Groups page has up to three tabs, depending on your permissions:
Tab | What it shows
User Groups | A simple list of the groups defined in the survey.
Group Assignments | A Kanban-style board with one column per group (plus an "Unassigned" column) and one card per user; drag and drop a user’s card to change their group.
Members Report | A flat table with one row per group member, listing the group’s name, label and qualifiers alongside the member’s name, email, survey role and account status.

sections.title: Creating and Editing a User Group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
- On the User Groups tab, click New Group.
- Enter a Name for the group. The name is normalized automatically (no spaces or special characters) and it must be unique within the survey.
- Enter a Label for each survey language – this is the friendly name shown to users throughout Arena.
- Optionally add one or more Qualifiers (see 11.3.4) and select in Can view the records of the groups whose records the members can view (see 11.3.8).
- Click Save. Once the group is saved, a Members panel appears at the bottom of the page (see 11.3.5).
To edit an existing group, open it from the User Groups list and change any field, then click Save again. To remove a group, open it and click Delete; in this case the members are not deleted, they simply become unassigned.

sections.title: Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: A qualifier is a key/value pair attached to a group. The key must match the name of a survey attribute that has been marked as a qualifier attribute in the Form Designer (see 11.3.4.1). When this is done, Arena uses the pair to automatically fill in and restrict data for members of that group.

sections.title: Marking an attribute as a Qualifier
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be used as qualifiers. To enable one, do next:
- Open the Form Designer and select the text or code attribute (it must be defined inside the root level entity) that will hold the group value (for example, "region" or "project_code").
- In the attribute’s Basic Properties panel, enable the Qualifier checkbox. This option only appears once when at least one User Group exists in the survey.
What "Qualifier" does: When a new record is created by a user belonging to a group, this attribute is automatically filled with the value specified for it among that group’s qualifiers. Users will only be able to see and modify records belonging to their own group if they belong to one.

sections.title: Adding qualifier values to a group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Back on the group’s edit page, in the Qualifiers panel:
- Click Add qualifier.
- Under Key, enter the exact name of the qualifier attribute defined on the form (e.g. "region").
- Under Value, enter the value that should apply to this group (e.g. "North"; for a Code attribute, enter the item’s code).
- Repeat for additional qualifier attributes, and then click Save.
A group can have several qualifiers if the form defines several qualifier attributes. Each qualifier key must be unique within the group, and it cannot be left blank.

sections.title: Effect on data entry and data access
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
- New record: the qualifier attribute(s) are filled in automatically as soon as a member of the group starts collecting a new record, using the value(s) set on their group.
- Existing records: a user can only view and edit records whose qualifier attribute value matches their own group’s qualifier value. Attempts to open or edit a record outside their group are rejected.
- Unassigned users, or groups without a matching qualifier, are not restricted by this mechanism.
- Guests: the members of the group with the Guest role can view the records of their group (and of the groups selected in Can view the records of, see 11.3.8), also in Arena Mobile, but they cannot edit them, nor add new records.
- A user is considered to belong to at most one group per survey; only that group’s qualifiers are applied.

sections.title: Managing Group Members
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: There are two ways to assign survey users to a group. These are explained next.

sections.title: Method 1. From the group’s edit page
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
- Open the group and scroll to the Members panel.
- Use the Add member dropdown to pick up a survey user by name and email.
- If the chosen user already belongs to a different group, Arena asks for confirmation before moving them (a user can only be a member of one group at a time).
- To remove a member, click the ✕ icon next to their name. They become unassigned, not deleted from the survey.

sections.title: Method 2. From the Group Assignments board (drag and drop)
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The Group Assignments tab (visible only to users who can manage groups) shows every survey user as a card on a Kanban-style board, with one column per group plus a leading Unassigned column.
- Go to Users > User Groups > Group Assignments.
- Drag a user’s card from its current column into the column of the group you want to assign them to (or into Unassigned to remove them from any group).
The new status is saved immediately; there is no separate Save step for this view.

sections.title: Members Report
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: The Members Report tab gives a flat, exportable-style view for auditing group membership: one row per group/member pair, showing the group’s name, label and qualifiers next to the member’s name, email, survey role and account status (Invited, Accepted, or Password change required). Groups with no members still appear, with a single empty-member row, so no group is missed.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
- Can a user belong to more than one group?
No. Adding a user to a group who already belongs to a different group moves them to the new group after a confirmation prompt.
- What happens to a group’s members if the group is deleted?
They are not removed from the survey; they simply become unassigned and lose any qualifier restriction that the group applied.
- Can I use a multiple-choice or nested attribute as a qualifier?
No. Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be marked as qualifiers.

sections.title: Read-only access to the records of other groups
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The members of a group with qualifiers can see and edit only the records of their own group. To let them also view the records of other groups (e.g. a supervisors' team), open the group and select those groups in Can view the records of, then click Save.
The members of the group can then view, export and download (also in Arena Mobile) the records of the selected groups, but they cannot edit them. In the example of section 11.3.3, the members of the Morogoro team can view the records of the Arusha team.
Record files, data exports and the records uploaded from Arena Mobile are also restricted to the records that the user group can access.

sections.title: Examples of expressions
sections.text:
Arena uses Javascript programming language for expressions. Because some users may be familiar with XPath language expressions used in OF Collect, the tables (use the link below) represent expressions with both these languages.
The filters of the Data Explorer and of the Validation report also use JavaScript syntax only. To search text values use includes, startsWith or endsWith, e.g. remarks.includes('dead'); add .toLowerCase() before them to ignore the case, e.g. remarks.toLowerCase().includes('dead').
Note: In JavaScript, a string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single (‘) or double (") quotes. The choice of quoting style is up to the programmer.
Operands (see more here): AND: && OR : || NOT: ! Equal to: == not equal: != Less than: <, <= Greater than: >, >= Multiplication: * , Division: / , Modulo: % , Exponentiation: **
All examples of expressions you can find in this online document. It contains the following topics:
12.1. "Relevant if" and "Apply if" rules 12.2. Methods and functions 12.3. Data validation 12.4. Functions using current user 12.5. Functions using current record 12.6. Examples 12.7. Items filter expressions
How to avoid performance issues with Arena / Arena Mobile
If you encounter slowness while editing a large number of entities in a multiple entity (table), you should check the expressions set in for every attribute (default values, validation rules, etc.), because, depending on the way they are defined, they can be evaluated by Arena and Arena Mobile too many times. This can happen when you record a new entity or delete an existing one.
Please follow these rules:
- when you have a default value with an expression that depends on the "index" of the entity, like index($context) + 1, mark it with "Default value evaluated only one time", otherwise the expression will be evaluated repeatedly every time you insert a new entity;
- when you have a validation rule that checks the value of an attribute, please prefer the use of "this" instead of the name of the variable; e.g. this > 10 instead of attribute_name > 10 or parent_entity_name.attribute_name > 10
- When you point at another attribute (e.g. this < tree_height_top), make sure that the attribute (tree_height_top) precedes in the data structure.

sections.title: System administration
Backup and restore users
sections.text:
You can copy the users from one Arena server to another one. In Users list (all), click Backup / Restore:
- Backup users exports the users with their survey roles and user groups (2FA devices are not exported). Choose which users to export: All users, the Selected users (select them with the checkbox in the first column of the list: the selection is kept when changing page or searching) or the Users with these emails (type or paste the email addresses, one per line or separated by commas). Select Include passwords to include the password hashes: in this case keep the backup file in a safe place and delete it after use.
- Restore users reads a backup file in the other server. Users are matched by email; survey roles and user groups are matched by survey name and group name, and the roles of surveys not existing in the server are ignored. For each user you can choose the action: Add (new users), Skip, Update survey roles or Update survey roles and details, and whether to restore the Password stored in the backup. If the passwords are not included in the backup, new users will have to reset their password.

sections.title: Login providers
sections.text:
In System Administration > Login Providers, system administrators configure the external login providers (Google, Microsoft or any OpenID Connect provider, such as Keycloak, Okta or the single sign-on of an organization). Their buttons are shown on the login page in the order of the list: use the arrows to change it.
To add a provider:
- Click Add provider, choose the type (Google, Microsoft or OpenID Connect) and click Continue.
- At the provider (e.g. Google Cloud console, Microsoft Entra admin center, Keycloak), register Arena as a web application and add the Redirect URI shown in the right panel of the form. The panel also lists the setup steps and links to a detailed guide for the provider type.
- Fill in the Button label, the Identifier (it cannot be changed later; google or microsoft is suggested for those types), the Client ID and Client secret given by the provider and, for OpenID Connect, the Issuer URL (for Microsoft, the Tenant), then click Save.
Other settings of a provider:
- Allowed email domains: choose Allow all email domains, or Allow only specific domains and add the domains (e.g. example.org) one by one or pasted as a list; at least one is required. Only the accounts with these email domains can then use the provider.
- Require Arena two-factor authentication: users who enabled 2FA must still enter their code; turn it off only if the provider requires its own multi-factor authentication.
- Trust emails from this provider: links accounts by email even when the provider does not confirm that the email is verified.
- Show on the login page: when unchecked, the provider has no button on the login page and users sign in with it using the direct link shown in the information of the option (e.g. https://arena.example.org/auth/oidc/org-sso).
Test connection checks that Arena can reach the provider; Test sign-in signs you in at the provider and shows the data it returns and the Arena user that would match, without logging you in. Disable hides the button and refuses the sign-ins with the provider, keeping the linked accounts; Delete removes the provider and its links, and emails the users left without any sign-in method how to set a password.
The server must have an encryption key for the client secrets (AUTH_PROVIDER_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY) and its public address (ARENA_PUBLIC_URL). Providers can also be defined in the server configuration (AUTH_PROVIDERS_CONFIG): they are shown read-only.

sections.title: System architecture
sections.text:
OF Arena is built with JavaScript programming language and the system is based on the following components:
- Static front-end in React.js
- Back-end in Node.js
- Database Management System: PostgreSQL
- Amazon Web Services (AWS),
- Leaflet JavaScript library for interactive maps,
- System front-end and back-end will communicate via Web Socket connection, and the OF Arena authentication system uses local user storage. OF Arena sends notifications via email.
- External data: users can upload files into the system,
- OF Arena integrates with RStudio server,
- Local off-line installation and usage via docker.
OF Arena uses cookies, so they should be allowed in the web browser. The system is tested with the following web browsers: Google Chrome (recommended), Windows Edge and Opera.

sections.title: RStudio Server: writing and downloading files created during run-time
sections.text:
Because RStudio Server works on a remote server, getting files, such as CSV files or graphic files, created by the R scripts from the server to the user’s machine requires special methods. Here we go through how to do this.
- Write this script into 000-common.R:
# define a folder for output files
user_file_path <- './user_output/'
# create a folder for files to be exported
if (!dir.exists( user_file_path )) dir.create( user_file_path, showWarnings = FALSE )
cat( normalizePath(user_file_path) )
Optionally, you can also use a function to add all "user’s files" into a zip file (arena_R_export.zip) which can be downloaded (after running the project files). Add also this script into 000-common.R (after the script above):
zip_user_files <- function(tFolder) {
#delete zip if it exists (i.e., file to be downloaded)
fn <- paste0( tFolder, "arena_R_export.zip ")
if (file.exists(fn)) {
#Delete file if it exists
file.remove(fn)
}
# check if any files to be zipped
f <- list.files(tFolder, all.files=TRUE, recursive=TRUE, full.names=FALSE)
if (length(f) > 0) {
zip::zip("arena_R_export.zip", f, recurse=TRUE , root=tFolder, include_directories = TRUE, mode = "mirror")
}
}
Note: add script zip_user_files( user_file_path ) into the very last calculation step.
- in the part where you need to write something into a CSV file, use this type of command line
write.csv(my_DF, paste0( user_file_path, "test.csv" ), row.names = FALSE)
- To download the files from the server, there are two methods: a) using RStudio’s EXPORT tool (this is easier), b) or by R coding.
a) RStudio’s EXPORT tool:
In the Files pane, More menu, there is an Export… option:
b) Coding method to export the files from the server:
file_list = list.files(path=user_file_path, pattern="*.csv")
for (i in seq_along(file_list)) {
export_filename = file_list[[i]]
# create a path for file to export
my_export_file_path <- paste0(user_file_path, export_filename)
# make a pause before exporting the next file, otherwise there can be a pop-up warning
if (i > 1) {
cat('*** PRESS ENTER HERE')
readLines(stdin(), 1)
}
# export to local disk using browser's capabilities
browseURL(my_export_file_path)
}

sections.title: Installing Open Foris Arena on a Custom Server (1/2)
sections.text:
This section explains how to install and run Open Foris Arena on your own server (on-premises or cloud VM) using Docker, instead of using the hosted openforis-arena.org platform. It is intended for system administrators who will maintain the server.
1. Overview
Arena is distributed as a set of Docker images: the Arena application itself, a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database, and, optionally, an RStudio Server container used for running custom R scripts on collected data. Running Arena on a custom server therefore requires Docker and, unless you already have one, a PostgreSQL database.
2. Prerequisites
- A server (Linux is recommended) with a public or reachable IP address, if the server must be accessed outside the local network.
- Docker installed. Download and install it from docker.com if it is not already present.
- Sufficient disk space for the database, uploaded files, and analysis output directories.
- Network access from the server to the internet, to pull Docker images (or a local copy of the images if the server is offline).
- Optional: an SMTP or SendGrid/Office365/Amazon SES account, if Arena should send emails (e.g., password resets, survey invitations).
3. Install and configure PostgreSQL
If you do not already have a PostgreSQL database available, run one as a Docker container. The following command creates a database named "arena" and a user "arena" with password "arena", listening on port 5444:
docker run -d --name arena-db -p 5444:5432 \ -e POSTGRES_DB=arena \ -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=arena \ -e POSTGRES_USER=arena \ postgis/postgis:17-3.5
Note: Change the database name, user, password, and port to suit your environment and security requirements. Arena can also be pointed at an already-existing PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance instead of a dedicated container.
4. Create the configuration file (arena.env)
Create a text file named arena.env containing the parameters Arena needs at startup. The most commonly used variables are listed below; the full list is available in the Arena GitHub repository.
Variable | Purpose | Example
ARENA_PORT | Port the web application listens on | 9090
PGHOST / PGPORT / PGDATABASE / PGUSER / PGPASSWORD | PostgreSQL connection parameters (or use DATABASE_URL) | localhost / 5444 / arena / arena / arena
TEMP_FOLDER | Folder for temporary uploaded files | /home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload
FILE_STORAGE_PATH | File-system folder for stored files (omit to use DB or S3) | /home/your_user/openforis/arena/files
ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR | Folder shared with RStudio Server for analysis output | /home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis
USE_HTTPS | Set to true if requests are forwarded to HTTPS by a reverse proxy | false
ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD | Credentials for the first system administrator account | admin@example.org / temporary-password
A minimal working arena.env looks like this:
ARENA_PORT=9090 PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=5444 PGDATABASE=arena PGUSER=arena PGPASSWORD=arena TEMP_FOLDER=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/files ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis USER_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-string USE_HTTPS=false ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.org ADMIN_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-temporary-password
Security: ADMIN_PASSWORD is used only to create the first system administrator account. Change this password from within Arena immediately after the first login, and consider removing it from the file afterward.
5. Install and run Arena
From the folder containing arena.env, run:
docker run --env-file ./arena.env --network="host" openforis/arena:latest
This pulls the official Arena image and starts the container, exposing the web application on the port defined by ARENA_PORT (9090 by default). Use the same command to restart Arena after it has been stopped.
6. Open Arena in the browser
Once the container is running, open:
http://localhost:9090

On first startup, Arena automatically creates a system administrator account using ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from arena.env. Log in with those credentials and change the password using the Change Password function inside Arena.
7. Optional: run RStudio Server for statistical analysis
To enable custom R scripts and calculation chains, run RStudio Server as a separate container, sharing the ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR folder defined in arena.env:
docker run -d --name arena-rstudio --network=host \ -v ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR:/home/rstudio \ -e DISABLE_AUTH=true \ rocker/rstudio
Replace ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR with the actual path used in arena.env. RStudio Server will be available at:
http://localhost:8787
To restart RStudio Server after a reboot or stop:
docker container restart arena-rstudio
Alternatively, an already-existing external RStudio Server (or RStudio Server Pro pool) can be connected by setting RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL (and related RSTUDIO_* variables) in arena.env instead of running a local container.
8. Recommended next steps
- Configure HTTPS via a reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx or Traefik) in front of Arena, and set USE_HTTPS=true in arena.env.
- Set up an email service (SendGrid, Office365, or Amazon SES) so Arena can send account and survey-invitation emails.
- Schedule regular backups of the PostgreSQL database and the file-storage / analysis directories.
- Review the ALLOW_USER_ACCESS_REQUEST, FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT, and JOB_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY settings to match your organization's needs.
